  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank&#8217;s ability to compete effectively is a result of being able to provide customers with desired products and services in a convenient and cost effective manner.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Customers for commercial, consumer and mortgage banking as well as trust services are influenced by convenience, quality of service, personal contacts, availability of products and services and related pricing.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank continually reviews its products, locations, alternative delivery channels and pricing strategies to maintain and enhance its competitive position.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management believes it can compete effectively as a result of local market knowledge and awareness of, and attention to, customer needs.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Employees</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 30.25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2013, the Bank had 301 full-time employees and 70 part-time employees.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank believes that relations with its employees are good.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>None of the employees of the Bank are represented by a labor union or subject to a collective bargaining agreement.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Regulation and Supervision</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 30.25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following discussion describes elements of an extensive regulatory framework applicable to bank holding companies and banks and specific information about BKFC.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Federal and state regulation of banks and their holding companies is intended primarily for the protection of depositors and the Deposit Insurance Fund (&#8220;DIF&#8221;), rather than for the protection of shareholders and creditors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A change in statutes, regulations or policies could have a material impact on the business of BKFC and its subsidiaries, including changes resulting from the passage of the Dodd-Frank Act in 2010 and the implementation of rulemaking under the Dodd-Frank Act that has continued through 2013, as described in more detail below.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BKFC and its subsidiaries may also be affected by future legislation and rulemaking that can change banking statutes in substantial and unexpected ways and by the actions of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the &#8220;FRB&#8221;) as it attempts to control the money supply and credit availability in order to influence the economy.<U></U></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Regulation of BKFC</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BKFC is a bank holding company subject to regulation by the FRB under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (&#8220;BHCA&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As a bank holding company, BKFC is required to file periodic reports with, and is subject to the regulation, supervision and examination by, the FRB.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such examination by the FRB determines whether BKFC is operating in accordance with various regulatory requirements and in a safe and sound manner.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The FRB may initiate enforcement proceedings against BKFC for violations of laws or regulations or for engaging in unsafe and unsound practices, particularly if such conduct could or does adversely impact the Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BKFC is also subject to the disclosure and regulatory requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, as administered by the SEC.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 30.25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under the BHCA, the FRB&#8217;s prior approval is required in any case in which BKFC proposes to acquire all or substantially all of the assets of any bank, acquire direct or indirect ownership or control of more than 5% of the voting shares of any bank, or merge or consolidate with any other bank holding company.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The BHCA also prohibits, with certain exceptions, BKFC from acquiring direct or indirect ownership or control of more than 5% of any class of voting shares of any non-banking company.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under the BHCA, BKFC may not engage in any business other than managing and controlling banks or furnishing certain specified services to subsidiaries and may not acquire voting control of non-banking companies unless the FRB determines such businesses and services to be closely related to banking.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>When reviewing bank acquisition applications for approval, the FRB considers, among other things, each subsidiary bank&#8217;s record in meeting the credit needs of the communities it serves in accordance with the Community Reinvestment Act of 1977, as amended (the &#8220;CRA&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank has a current CRA rating of &#8220;satisfactory.&#8221;<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, the FRB could require that BKFC terminate any activity, if the FRB deems the activity to constitute a serious risk to the financial soundness of the Bank. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">It is the policy of the FRB that a bank holding company be ready and able to use its resources to provide capital to its subsidiary banks during periods of financial stress or adversity.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The FRB could require BKFC to provide such support at times when BKFC lacks the resources to do so.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>See &#8220;Regulatory Capital Requirements&#8221; and &#8220;Dividend Restrictions&#8221; regarding minimum capital levels to which BKFC is subject and regulatory limits on BKFC&#8217;s ability to pay dividends to shareholders.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As a bank holding company, BKFC must notify the FRB if, during any one-year period, it seeks to redeem shares of stock in an amount such that total redemptions during the year, net of sales of shares, would be greater than 10% of BKFC&#8217;s net worth. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Regulation of the Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank is a Kentucky-chartered bank with FDIC deposit insurance.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank is subject to numerous federal and state statutes and regulations regarding the conduct of its business, including, among other things, maintenance of reserves against deposits; capital adequacy; restrictions on the nature and amount of loans which may be made and the interest which may be charged thereon; restrictions on the terms of loans to officers, directors, large shareholders and their affiliates; restrictions relating to investments and other activities; and requirements regarding mergers and branching activities.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>

style="WIDTH: 100%">

style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank is subject to the regulation, supervision and examination by the Department and the FDIC.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Both the Department and the FDIC have the authority to issue cease-and-desist orders if either determines that the activities of the Bank represent unsafe and unsound banking practices.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If the grounds provided by law exist, the Department or the FDIC may appoint a conservator or receiver for the Bank.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">State-chartered banks, like the Bank, are subject to regulatory oversight under various consumer protection and fair lending laws.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These laws govern, among other things, truth-in-lending disclosure, equal credit opportunity, fair credit reporting and community reinvestment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Failure to abide by federal laws and regulations governing community reinvestment could limit the ability of a state-chartered bank to open a new branch or engage in a merger transaction.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank is subject to the guidance on sound risk management practices for concentrations in commercial real estate lending set forth by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the FRB and the FDIC.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The guidance is intended to help ensure that institutions pursuing a significant commercial real estate lending strategy remain healthy and profitable while continuing to serve the credit needs of their communities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Also, this guidance directs institutions in developing risk management practices and levels of capital that are commensurate with the level and nature of their commercial real estate concentrations.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Kentucky law limits loans or other extensions of credit to any borrower to 20% of the Bank&#8217;s paid-in capital and actual surplus.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such limit is increased to 30% if the borrower provides good collateral security or executes to it a mortgage upon real or personal property with a cash value exceeding the amount of the loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans or extensions of credit to certain borrowers are aggregated, and loans secured by certain government obligations are exempt from these limits.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, the maximum the Bank could lend to any one borrower generally equaled $23 million and equaled $34 million if the borrower provided collateral with a cash value in excess of the amount of the loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Federal banking laws and regulations also limit the transfer of funds or other items of value, including pursuant to the provision of loans, from banks to their affiliates.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Generally, the Bank&#8217;s permissible activities and investments are prescribed by Kentucky law.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, state-chartered banks, including the Bank, may not, directly or through a subsidiary, engage in activities or make any investments as principal not permitted for a national bank, a bank holding company or a subsidiary of a nonmember bank, unless they obtain FDIC approval.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Dodd-Frank Act.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Dodd-Frank Act represents a significant overhaul of many aspects of the regulation of the financial-services industry.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Dodd-Frank Act implements numerous and far-reaching changes that affect financial companies, including banks and bank holding companies such as BKFC by, among other things:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <TABLE

style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%">
    <TR>  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="left">

  <TD
style="FONT-STYLE: normal; WIDTH: 34%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" align="center">
18</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="right">

  <TR>  <TD><BR /></TD>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 2px solid; FONT-STYLE: normal; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
The majority of the provisions in the Dodd-Frank Act are aimed at financial institutions that are significantly larger than BKFC or the Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Nonetheless, there are provisions with which we will have to comply now that the Dodd-Frank Act is signed into law. Many aspects of the Dodd-Frank Act are subject to further rulemaking and will take effect over several years, making it difficult to anticipate the overall financial impact on BKFC and the Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, compliance with this law and its implementing regulations has resulted, and will continue to result, in additional operating costs that could have a material adverse effect on our future financial condition and results of operations.</DIV>
</FONT>  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 (the &#8220;EESA&#8221;) was enacted on October 3, 2008.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The EESA authorized the Secretary of the Treasury Department (the &#8220;Secretary&#8221;) to purchase or guarantee up to $700 billion in troubled assets from financial institutions under TARP.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Pursuant to authority granted under the EESA, the Secretary created the TARP CPP under which the Treasury Department was authorized to invest up to $250 billion in senior preferred stock of U.S. banks and savings associations or their holding companies.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Treasury Department&#8217;s authority to make new investments under the CPP expired in October 2010.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CPP Participation.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On February 13, 2009, BKFC issued 34,000 shares of Series A Preferred Stock for a total price of $34 million pursuant to a Letter Agreement with the Treasury Department (the &#8220;Purchase Agreement&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On November 23, 2011, BKFC repurchased the final $17 million outstanding Series A Preferred Stock held by the Treasury Department.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Accordingly, BKFC no longer is subject to the restrictions applicable to CPP participants.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As part of its purchase of the Series A Preferred Stock, the Treasury Department received the Warrant to purchase 274,784 shares of Common Stock at an initial per share exercise price of $18.56, which was repurchased in the second quarter of 2013.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Both the Series A Preferred Stock and the Warrant were accounted for as components of Tier 1 capital. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Regulatory Capital Requirements.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The FRB has adopted risk-based capital guidelines for bank holding companies.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such companies must maintain adequate consolidated capital to meet the minimum ratio of total capital to risk-weighted assets (including certain off-balance-sheet items, such as standby letters of credit) (the &#8220;Total Risk-Based Ratio&#8221;) of 8%.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At least half of the minimum-required total capital of 8% must be composed of Tier 1 Capital, which consists of common shareholders&#8217; equity, minority interests in the equity of consolidated subsidiaries and a limited amount of perpetual preferred stock, less goodwill and certain other intangibles (&#8220;Tier 1 Risk-Based Ratio&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The remainder of total capital may consist of subordinated and qualifying convertible debt, other preferred stock and a limited amount of loan and lease loss allowances.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The FRB also has established minimum leverage ratio guidelines for bank holding companies.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The guidelines provide for a minimum ratio of Tier 1 Capital to average total assets (excluding the loan and lease loss allowance, goodwill and certain other intangibles, and portions of certain nonfinancial equity investments) (the &#8220;Leverage Ratio&#8221;) of 3% for bank holding companies that meet specified criteria, including having the highest regulatory rating.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>All other bank holding companies must maintain a Leverage Ratio of 4% to 5%.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The guidelines further provide that bank holding companies making acquisitions are expected to maintain strong capital positions substantially above the minimum supervisory levels.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank is subject to similar capital requirements, and such capital requirements are imposed and enforced by the FDIC.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As part of the Dodd-Frank Act, provisions were added that require federal banking agencies to develop capital requirements that address systemically risky activities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The effect of these capital rules are such that trust preferred securities issued by a company, such as BKFC, with total consolidated assets of less than $15 billion before May 19, 2010 and treated as regulatory capital are grandfathered, but any such securities issued later are not eligible as regulatory capital.&#160;&#160;The banking regulators must develop regulations setting minimum risk-based and leverage capital requirements for holding companies and banks on a consolidated basis that are no less stringent than the generally applicable requirements in effect for depository institutions under the prompt corrective action regulations discussed below.&#160;&#160;The banking regulators also must seek to make capital standards countercyclical so that the required levels of capital increase in times of economic expansion and decrease in times of economic contraction.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%">
    <TR>  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="left">
</TD>

style="FONT-STYLE: normal; WIDTH: 34%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" align="center">
19</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="right">

style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Basel</FONT></B><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> III.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>In 2010, the Group of Governors and Heads of Supervisors of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, the oversight body of the Basel Committee, published its &#8220;calibrated&#8221; capital standards for major banking institutions (&#8220;Basel III&#8221;). Under these standards, when fully phased in, banking institutions will be required to maintain heightened Tier&#160;1 common equity, Tier&#160;1 capital and total capital ratios, as well as maintaining a &#8220;capital conservation buffer.&#8221; As proposed, Basel III provides for the Tier 1 common equity and Tier 1 capital ratio requirements to be phased in incrementally between January 1, 2013 and January 1, 2015; the deductions from common equity made in calculating Tier 1 common equity (for example, for mortgage servicing assets, deferred tax assets and investments in unconsolidated financial institutions) to be phased in incrementally over a four-year period commencing on January 1, 2014; and the capital conservation buffer to be phased in incrementally between January 1, 2016 and January 1, 2019.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Basel Committee also announced that a &#8220;countercyclical buffer&#8221; of 0% to 2.5% of common equity or other fully loss-absorbing capital &#8220;will be implemented according to national circumstances&#8221; as an &#8220;extension&#8221; of the conservation buffer.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The final package of Basel III reforms was approved by the G20 leaders in November 2010 and is subject to individual adoption by member nations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>While Basel III is intended to be implemented on a global basis beginning January 1, 2013, it was not until July 2, 2013, that the United States, through the FRB and the OCC, adopted final rules for U.S. Banking organizations implementing Basel III requirements (the &#8220;Final Rules&#8221;).</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">U.S.</FONT></B><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> Implementation of Basel III.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Final Rules establish a comprehensive capital framework and will implement the Basel III reforms and certain changes required by the Dodd-Frank Act. Under the Final Rules, minimum requirements will increase for both the quantity and quality of capital held by banking organizations. Consistent with the international Basel III framework, the Final Rules include a new minimum ratio of common equity tier 1 capital (Tier 1 Common) to risk-weighted assets and a Tier 1 Common capital conservation buffer of 2.5% of risk-weighted assets that will apply to all supervised financial institutions. The Final Rules also raise the minimum ratio of tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets and includes a minimum leverage ratio of 4% for all banking organizations. These new minimum capital ratios will become effective for us on January 1, 2015, and will be fully phased-in on January 1, 2019. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Following are the Basel III regulatory capital levels that we must satisfy to avoid limitations on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments during the applicable transition period, from January 1, 2015 until January 1, 2019:</FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">

  <TD
style="FONT-STYLE: normal; WIDTH: 34%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" align="center">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;BACKGROUND-COLOR: rgb(0,0,0); FONT-STYLE: normal; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The FDIC may require an increase in a bank&#8217;s risk-based capital requirements on an individualized basis to address the bank&#8217;s exposure to a decline in the economic value of its capital due to a change in interest rates, among other things.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Prompt Corrective Regulatory Action.</FONT></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The FDIC has adopted regulations governing prompt corrective action to resolve the problems of capital deficient and otherwise troubled banks under its regulation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For these purposes, the law establishes three categories of capital deficient institutions: undercapitalized, significantly undercapitalized and critically undercapitalized.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At each successively lower defined capital category, an institution is subject to more restrictive and numerous mandatory or discretionary regulatory actions or limits, and the FDIC has less flexibility in determining how to resolve the problems of the institution.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The FDIC generally can downgrade an institution&#8217;s capital category, notwithstanding its capital level, if, after notice and opportunity for hearing, the institution is deemed to be engaging in an unsafe or unsound practice because it has not corrected deficiencies that resulted in it receiving a less than satisfactory examination rating on matters other than capital or it is deemed to be in an unsafe or unsound condition.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>An undercapitalized institution must submit a capital restoration plan to the FDIC within 45 days after it becomes undercapitalized.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such institution will be subject to increased monitoring and asset growth restrictions and will be required to obtain prior approval for acquisitions, branching and engaging in new lines of business.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Furthermore, critically undercapitalized institutions must be placed in conservatorship or receivership within 270 days of reaching that capitalization level, except under limited circumstances.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At year-end 2013, the most recent regulatory notifications categorized the Bank as well capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>There are no conditions or events since that notification that management believes have changed the institution's category. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The FDIC has adopted regulations to implement the prompt corrective action legislation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>An institution is deemed to be &#8220;well capitalized&#8221; if it has a Total Risk-Based Ratio of 10% or greater, a Tier 1 Risk-Based Ratio of 6% or greater, and a Leverage Ratio of 5% or greater.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>An institution is &#8220;adequately capitalized&#8221; if it has a Total Risk-Based Ratio of 8% or greater, a Tier 1 Risk-Based Ratio of 4% or greater and generally a Leverage Ratio of 4% or greater.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>An institution is &#8220;undercapitalized&#8221; if it has a Total Risk-Based Ratio of less than 8%, a Tier 1 Risk-Based Ratio of less than 4%, or generally a Leverage Ratio of less than 4% (3% or less for institutions with the highest examination rating).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>An institution is deemed to be &#8220;significantly undercapitalized&#8221; if it has a Total Risk-Based Ratio of less than 6%, a Tier 1 Risk-Based Ratio<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>of less than 3%, or a Leverage Ratio of less than 3%.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>An institution is considered to be &#8220;critically undercapitalized&#8221; if it has a ratio of tangible equity (as defined in the regulations) to total assets that is equal to or less than 2%. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Basel III capital rules revise the &#8220;prompt corrective action&#8221; directives by (i) introducing a Tier 1 common equity ratio requirement at each level (other than critically undercapitalized), with the required Tier 1 common equity ratio being 6.5% for well-capitalized status; (ii) increasing the minimum Tier 1 capital ratio requirement for each category, with the minimum Tier 1 capital ratio for well-capitalized status being 8% (compared with the current 6%); and (iii) eliminating the current provision that provides that a bank with a composite supervisory rating of 1 may have a 3% leverage ratio and still be adequately capitalized. The Basel III Capital Rules do not change the total risk-based capital requirement for any &#8220;prompt corrective action&#8221; category.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank&#8217;s capital levels at December 31, 2013 met the standards for the highest level, a &#8220;well-capitalized&#8221; institution.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Federal law prohibits a financial institution from making a capital distribution to anyone or paying management fees to any person having control of the institution if, after such distribution or payment, the institution would be undercapitalized.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, each holding company controlling an undercapitalized institution must guarantee that the institution will comply with its capital restoration plan until the institution has been adequately capitalized on an average during each of the four preceding calendar quarters and must provide adequate assurances of performance.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The aggregate liability pursuant to such guarantee is limited to the lesser of (i) an amount equal to 5% of the institution&#8217;s total assets at the time it became undercapitalized or (ii) the amount necessary to bring the institution into compliance with all capital standards applicable to such institution at the time the institution fails to comply with its capital restoration plan.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Dividend Restrictions.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT>There are a number of statutory and regulatory requirements applicable to the payment of dividends by banks and bank holding companies.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Please see Note 16 of the financial statements for a discussion on the Bank&#8217;s current dividend restrictions.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">If the FRB or the FDIC determines that a bank holding company or a bank is engaged in or is about to engage in an unsafe or unsound practice (which, depending on the financial condition of the entity, could include the payment of dividends), that regulator may require, after notice and hearing, that such bank holding company or bank cease and desist from such practice.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, the FRB and the FDIC have issued policy statements, which provide that insured banks and bank holding companies should generally only pay dividends out of current operating earnings.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The FDIC prohibits the payment of any dividend by a bank that would constitute an unsafe or unsound practice.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Compliance with the minimum capital requirements limits the amounts that BKFC and the Bank can pay as dividends.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2013, BKFC paid a cash dividend of $0.69 per share totaling approximately $5.2 million on common stock. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FDIC Deposit Insurance and Assessments.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The FDIC is an independent federal agency that insures deposits, up to prescribed statutory limits, of federally insured banks and thrifts and safeguards the safety and soundness of the banking and thrift industries.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank&#8217;s deposits are insured by the DIF.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The DIF is the successor to the Bank Insurance Fund and the Savings Association Insurance Fund, which were merged in 2006.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The FDIC amended its risk-based assessment system to implement authority granted by the Federal Deposit Insurance Reform Act of 2005.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under the revised system, insured institutions are assigned to one of four risk categories based on supervisory evaluations, regulatory capital levels and certain other factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>An institution&#8217;s assessment rate depends upon the category to which it is assigned.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Risk Category I, which contains the least risky depository institutions, is expected to include 90% of all institutions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Unlike the other categories, Risk Category I contains further risk differentiation based on the FDIC&#8217;s analysis of financial ratios, examination component ratings and other information.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In October 2008, the basic limit on federal deposit insurance coverage of interest bearing transaction accounts was temporarily increased from $100,000 to $250,000 per depositor under the EESA, which was subsequently made permanent under the Dodd-Frank Act. In October 2008, the FDIC announced TLGP which provided full coverage for noninterest-bearing transaction accounts at FDIC-insured institutions that agreed to participate in the program through December 31, 2010.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank participated in this program. In July 2010, the Dodd-Frank Act extended unlimited FDIC insurance coverage for non-interest-bearing transaction deposit accounts for an additional two years. This unlimited insurance coverage for noninterest-bearing transaction accounts expired on December 31, 2012.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 12, 2009, the FDIC adopted regulations that require all depository institutions to prepay on December 30, 2009 their estimated risk-based insurance assessments for the fourth quarter of 2009, and for all of 2010, 2011 and 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At that same time, institutions were also required to pay their regular quarterly assessments for the third quarter of 2009.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>An institution&#8217;s quarterly risk-based deposit insurance assessments thereafter would be paid from the amount the institution prepaid until that amount was exhausted or until June 30, 2013, when any amount remaining would be returned to the institution.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The prepaid assessment amount was $0 and $1,848,000 on December 30, 2013 and 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On July 1, 2013, the FDIC returned $1,159,000 to the Bank as the restoration plan came to an end.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pursuant to the Dodd-Frank Act, the FDIC has established 2.0% as the designated reserve ratio (&#8220;DRR&#8221;), that is, the ratio of the DIF to insured deposits. The FDIC has adopted a plan under which it will meet the statutory minimum DRR of 1.35% by September&#160;30, 2020, the deadline imposed by the Dodd-Frank Act.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Dodd-Frank Act requires the FDIC to offset the effect on institutions with assets less than $10 billion of the increase in the statutory minimum DRR to 1.35% from the former statutory minimum of 1.15%.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The FDIC has not yet announced how it will implement this offset.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As required by the Dodd-Frank Act, the FDIC has adopted rules which were effective April&#160;1, 2011, under which insurance premium assessments are based on an institution&#8217;s total assets minus its tangible equity (defined as Tier 1 capital) instead of its deposits.&#160; Under these rules, an institution with total assets of less than $10 billion, such as the Bank, will be assigned to a risk category as described above and a range of initial base assessment rates will apply to each category, subject to adjustment downward based on unsecured debt issued by the institution and, except for an institution in Risk Category I, adjustment upward if the institution&#8217;s brokered deposits exceed 10% of its domestic deposits, to produce total base assessment rates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The FDIC may increase or decrease its rates by 2.0 basis points without further rulemaking.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In an emergency, the FDIC may also impose a special assessment.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The FDIC may increase or decrease the assessment rate schedule from one quarter to the next. An increase in the assessment rate could have a material adverse effect on BKFC&#8217;s earnings, depending on the amount of the increase.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The FDIC is authorized to terminate a depository institution&#8217;s deposit insurance upon a finding by the FDIC that the institution&#8217;s financial condition is unsafe or unsound, or that the institution has engaged in unsafe or unsound practices, or has violated any applicable rule, regulation, order or condition enacted or imposed by the institution&#8217;s regulatory agency. The termination of deposit insurance for the Bank could have a material adverse effect on BKFC&#8217;s earnings<B>.</B></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 30.25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FRB Reserve Requirements.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>FRB regulations currently require banks to maintain reserves of 3% of net transaction accounts (primarily demand and NOW accounts) up to $79.5 million of such accounts (subject to an exemption of up to $12.4 million), and of 10% of net transaction accounts in excess of $79.5 million.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2013, the Bank was in compliance with this reserve requirement, which was $11,643,000.</FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Acquisitions of Control.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT>Acquisitions of controlling interests of BKFC and the Bank are subject to the limitations in federal and state laws.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These limits generally require regulatory approval of acquisitions of specified levels of stock of any of these entities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Acquisitions of BKFC or the Bank by merger or pursuant to the purchase of assets also require regulatory approval.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 30.25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Federal Home Loan Banks.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The FHLBs provide credit to their members in the form of advances. The Bank is a member of the FHLB of Cincinnati and must maintain an investment in the capital stock of the FHLB of Cincinnati that consists of two components, the first is the membership component which is equal to 0.15% of the Bank&#8217;s total assets, and the second is an activity component that is equal to 2% to 4% of the Bank&#8217;s outstanding advances. The Bank is in compliance with this requirement with an investment in stock of the FHLB of Cincinnati of $5,099,000 at December 31, 2013 and 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Generally, FHLBs are not permitted to make new advances to a member without positive tangible capital.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Federal Taxation</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BKFC.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BKFC and the Bank file a consolidated federal income tax return on a calendar year basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BKFC is subject to the federal tax laws and regulations that apply to corporations generally.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In 2000, the Bank acquired the stock of FTFC.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>FTFC&#8217;s wholly owned subsidiary was FTSB.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Federal income tax laws provided savings banks with additional bad debt deductions through 1987, totaling $1,255,000 for FTFC.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Accounting standards do not require a deferred tax liability to be recorded on this amount, which would otherwise total $427,000.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Upon acquisition, this unrecorded liability was transferred to the Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If the Bank was liquidated or otherwise ceased to be a bank or if tax laws were to change, the $427,000 would be recorded as a liability with an offset to income tax expense.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2007, </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BKFC consummated the acquisition of <FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT>FNB Bancorporation, Inc. and its subsidiary, First Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The First Bank acquisition included a $13,748,000 net operating loss (&#8220;NOL&#8221;) carryforward which was set up as a $4,700,000 deferred tax asset.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>NOL carryforward will be deducted from income over the next 18 years in accordance to section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code.</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Kentucky Taxation </FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 31.7pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BKFC.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Kentucky corporations, such as BKFC, are subject to the Kentucky corporation income tax and the Kentucky corporation license (franchise) tax.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The income tax is imposed based on the following rates: 4% of the first $50,000 of taxable net income allocated or apportioned to Kentucky; 5% of the next $50,000; and 6% of taxable net income over $100,000.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>All dividend income received by a corporation is excluded for purposes of arriving at taxable net income.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Domestic corporations are subject to state and local ad valorem taxes on tangible personal property and real property that is not otherwise exempt from taxation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The rates of taxation for tangible personal property vary depending on the character of the property.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The state rate of taxation on real property equals $0.122 per $100 of value as of January 1 each year.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Thus, BKFC is subject to ad valorem taxation on its taxable tangible personal property and real property.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 31.7pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>State banks are not subject to the Kentucky corporation income tax. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 31.7pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Commonwealth of Kentucky imposes both a &#8220;Kentucky Bank Franchise Tax&#8221; and &#8220;Local Deposits Franchise Tax&#8221;.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The &#8220;Kentucky Bank Franchise Tax&#8221; is an annual tax equal to 1.1% of net capital after apportionment, if applicable.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The value of net capital is calculated annually by deducting from total capital an amount equal to the same percentage of the total as the book value of United States obligations bears to the book value of the total assets of the financial institution.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank pays a portion of its franchise tax to the state of Ohio based on revenue apportioned to that state. The &#8220;Local Deposits Franchise Tax&#8221; is an annual tax of up to 0.025% imposed by each city and county on bank deposits within their jurisdictions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 31.7pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Kentucky property tax extends to bank deposits (the&#8220;Deposits Tax&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The tax is levied at a rate of 0.00001% of the amount of the deposits.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It is the responsibility of the bank, not the depositor, to report and pay the Deposits Tax.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 31.7pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">State banks are subject to state and local ad valorem taxes on tangible personal property and real property that is not otherwise exempt from taxation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The rates of taxation for tangible personal property vary depending on the character of the property.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The state rate of taxation on real property equals $0.122 per $100 of value as of January 1 each year.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 31.7pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank, as a financial institution, is exempt from both the corporate income and license taxes.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Item 1A.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT>Risk Factors</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">An investment in the Common Stock of BKFC is subject to certain risks inherent in the business of BKFC and the Bank. The material risks and uncertainties that management believes affect BKFC and the Bank are described below. Before making an investment decision, you should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all of the other information included or incorporated by reference into this Annual Report. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones facing BKFC or the Bank. Additional risks and uncertainties that management is not aware of or focused on or that management currently deems immaterial may also impair the business operations of BKFC or the Bank. This Annual Report is qualified in its entirety by these risk factors.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">If any of the following risks occur, or if any combination of the following risks occur, the financial condition and results of operations of BKFC or the Bank could be materially and adversely affected. If this were to happen, the value of Common Stock could decline significantly.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">References to &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us,&#8221; and &#8220;our&#8221; in this &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; section refer to BKFC and its subsidiaries, including the Bank, unless otherwise specified or unless the context otherwise requires.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our business depends upon the general economic conditions of the northern Kentucky and greater Cincinnati, Ohio area, and may continue to be adversely affected by downturns in the local economies in which we operate.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our business operations are limited almost exclusively to the northern Kentucky and the greater Cincinnati, Ohio area, which is a small geographic area. As such, our business is closely tied to the general economic conditions of this area. Local economic conditions in this area have a significant impact on the demand for our products and services, as well as the ability of our customers to repay loans, the value of the collateral securing loans and the stability of the Bank&#8217;s deposit funding sources.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A significant decline in general economic conditions could increase loan delinquencies, increase problem assets and foreclosure, increase claims and lawsuits, decrease the demand for the Bank&#8217;s products and services, or decrease the value of collateral for loans, especially real estate, in turn reducing customers&#8217; borrowing power and the value of assets associated with problem loans and collateral coverage, thereby having a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A significant portion of our loans are secured by real estate and concentrated in the northern Kentucky and greater Cincinnati area, which may adversely affect our earnings and capital if real estate values decline.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Nearly 80% of our total loans are real estate interests (residential, nonresidential including both owner-occupied and investment real estate, and construction and land development) concentrated in the northern Kentucky area and neighboring areas in greater Cincinnati, Ohio, a small geographic area. As a result, declining real estate values in the northern Kentucky and greater Cincinnati, Ohio markets as a result of the ongoing national economic recession could negatively impact the value of the real estate collateral securing such loans. If we are required to liquidate a significant amount of collateral during a period of reduced real estate values in satisfaction of any non-performing or defaulted loans, our earnings and capital could be adversely affected.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We are subject to intense competition in our market area, and our business will be adversely affected if we are unable to compete effectively.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BKFC and the Bank compete with national financial institutions, as well as numerous state chartered banking institutions of comparable or larger size and resources, smaller community banking organizations and a variety of nonbank competitors. The Bank competes for deposits with other commercial banks, savings associations and credit unions and with the issuers of commercial paper and other securities, such as shares in money market mutual funds. In making loans, the Bank competes with other banks, savings associations, consumer finance companies, credit unions, leasing companies and other lenders. Many of the institutions against whom we compete are national and regional banks that are significantly larger than us and, therefore, have significantly greater resources and the ability to achieve economies of scale by offering a broader range of products and services at more competitive prices than we can offer. We expect competition to increase in the future as a result of legislative, regulatory and technological changes and the continuing trend of consolidation in the financial services industry.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our ability to compete successfully and to maintain and grow our profitability depends upon a number of factors, including:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>the ability to develop, maintain and build upon long-term customer relationships based on top-quality service, high ethical standards and safe, sound assets; the ability to continue to expand BKFC&#8217;s market position through organic growth and strategic acquisitions; the scope, relevance and pricing of products and services offered to meet customer needs and demands; the rate at which BKFC introduces new products and services relative to our competitors; and industry and general economic trends.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Failure to perform in any of these areas could significantly weaken our competitive position, which could adversely impact our financial condition and results of operations.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our nonresidential real estate loans expose us to greater risks of nonpayment and loss than residential mortgage loans, which may cause us to increase our allowance for loan losses which would reduce our net income.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2013, $571 million, or 46%, of our loan portfolio consisted of nonresidential real estate loans. Nonresidential real estate loans generally expose a lender to greater risk of non-payment and loss than residential mortgage loans because repayment of the loans often depends on the successful operation of the property and the income stream of the borrowers. Such loans expose us to additional risks because they typically are made on the basis of the borrower&#8217;s ability to make repayments from the cash flow of the borrower&#8217;s business and are secured by collateral that may depreciate over time. These loans typically involve larger loan balances to single borrowers or groups of related borrowers compared to residential mortgage loans. Because such loans generally entail greater risk than residential mortgage loans, we may need to increase our allowance for loan losses in the future to account for the likely increase in probable incurred credit losses associated with the growth of such loans, which would reduce our net income. Also, many of our nonresidential real estate borrowers have more than one loan outstanding with us. Consequently, an adverse development with respect to one loan or one credit relationship can expose us to a significantly greater risk of loss compared to an adverse development with respect to a residential mortgage loan.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A decline in general economic conditions could require additions to our allowance for loan losses, which would reduce our net income.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">If our borrowers do not repay their loans or if the collateral securing their loans is insufficient to provide for the full repayment, we may suffer credit losses. Credit losses are inherent in the lending business and could have a material adverse effect on our operating results. We make various assumptions and judgments about the collectability of our loan portfolio and provide an allowance for loan losses based on a number of factors. If our assumptions and judgments are wrong, our allowance for loan losses may not be sufficient to cover our losses. If we determine that our allowance for loan losses is insufficient, we would be required to take additional provisions for loan losses, which would reduce net income during the period those provisions are taken. In addition, our regulators periodically review our allowance for loan losses and may require us to increase our allowance for loan losses or to charge off particular loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If current economic trends change, we may experience higher than normal delinquencies and credit losses, resulting in increases to our provisions for loan losses again in the future and reduced net income.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Not all TDR&#8217;s are successful and may result in a higher allowance if they are evaluated on a collateral dependency basis.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our accounting policies and estimates are critical to how we report our financial condition and results of operations, and any changes to such accounting policies and estimates could materially affect how we report our financial condition and results of operations.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Accounting policies and estimates are fundamental to how we record and report our financial condition and results of operations. Our management makes judgments and assumptions in selecting and adopting various accounting policies and in applying estimates so that such policies and estimates comply with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;).</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management has identified certain accounting policies as being critical because they require management&#8217;s judgment to ascertain the valuations of assets, liabilities, commitments and contingencies.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A variety of factors could affect the ultimate value that is obtained either when earning income, recognizing an expense, recovering an asset, valuing an asset or liability or reducing a liability.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We have established detailed policies and control procedures that are intended to ensure that these critical accounting estimates and judgments are well controlled and applied consistently.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, these policies and procedures are intended to ensure that the process for changing methodologies occurs in an appropriate manner.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Because of the uncertainty surrounding our judgments and the estimates pertaining to these matters, actual outcomes may be materially different from amounts previously estimated.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For example, because of the inherent uncertainty of estimates, management cannot provide any assurance that the Bank will not significantly increase its allowance for loan losses if actual losses are more than the amount reserved.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Any increase in its allowance for loan losses or loan charge-offs could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, we cannot guarantee that we will not be required to adjust accounting policies or restate prior financial statements.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>See &#8220;Allowance for Loan Losses&#8221; under &#8220;Item 1. Business&#8221; and &#8220;Critical Accounting Policies&#8221; under &#8220;Item 7. Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8221; for additional discussion regarding these critical accounting policies. </FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Further, from time to time, the Financial Accounting Standards Board and SEC change the financial accounting and reporting standards that govern the preparation of our financial statements.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The ongoing economic recession has resulted in increased scrutiny of accounting standards by legislators and our regulators, particularly as they relate to fair value accounting principles.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, ongoing efforts to achieve convergence between GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards may result in changes to GAAP.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These changes can be hard to predict and can materially impact how we record and report our financial condition and results of operations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In some cases, we could be required to apply a new or revised standard retroactively, resulting in our restating prior period financial statements or otherwise adversely affecting our financial condition or results of operations.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
