<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our largest source of revenue (net interest income) is subject to interest rate risk.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank&#8217;s financial condition and results of operations are significantly affected by changes in interest rates. The Bank&#8217;s earnings depend primarily upon its net interest income, which is the difference between its interest income earned on its interest-earning assets, such as loans and investment securities, and its interest expense paid on its interest-bearing liabilities, consisting of deposits and borrowings. Moreover, the loans included in our interest-earning assets are primarily comprised of variable and adjustable rate loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Net interest income is subject to interest rate risk in the following ways:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <TABLE
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0pt; TABLE-LAYOUT: fixed; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; dtth: tableHanging" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
    <TR
style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 0pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; PADDING-TOP: 0in">
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 30pt; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 18.5pt; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Symbol; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#183;</FONT></FONT></TD>
  <TD
style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In general, for a given change in interest rates, the amount of change in value (positive or negative) is larger for assets and liabilities with longer remaining maturities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The shape of the yield curve may affect new loan yields, funding costs and investment income differently.</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <TABLE
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0pt; TABLE-LAYOUT: fixed; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; dtth: tableHanging" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
    <TR
style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 0pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; PADDING-TOP: 0in">
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 30pt; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 18.5pt; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Symbol; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#183;</FONT></FONT></TD>
  <TD
style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The remaining maturity of various assets or liabilities may shorten or lengthen as payment behavior changes in response to changes in interest rates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For example, if interest rates decline sharply, loans may pre-pay, or pay down, faster than anticipated, thus reducing future cash flows and interest income.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Conversely, if interest rates increase, depositors may cash in their certificates of deposit prior to maturity (notwithstanding any applicable early withdrawal penalties) or otherwise reduce their deposits to pursue higher yielding investment alternatives.</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <TABLE
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0pt; TABLE-LAYOUT: fixed; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; dtth: tableHanging" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
    <TR
style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 0pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; PADDING-TOP: 0in">
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 30pt; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 18.5pt; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Symbol; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#183;</FONT></FONT></TD>
  <TD
style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Re-pricing frequencies and maturity profiles for assets and liabilities may occur at different times.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For example, in a falling rate environment, if assets re-price faster than liabilities, there will be an initial decline in earnings.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Moreover, if assets and liabilities re-price at the same time, they may not be by the same increment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For instance, if the Federal Funds Rate increased 50 basis points, rates on demand deposits may rise by 10 basis points; whereas rates on prime-based loans will instantly rise 50 basis points.</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Financial instruments do not respond in a parallel fashion to rising or falling interest rates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This causes asymmetry in the magnitude of changes to net interest income, net economic value and investment income resulting from the hypothetical increases and decreases in interest rates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Therefore, BKFC&#8217;s management monitors interest rate risk and adjusts BKFC&#8217;s funding strategies to mitigate adverse effects of interest rate shifts on BKFC&#8217;s balance sheet.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank&#8217;s asset and liability management strategies designed to maintain a reasonable degree of interest rate sensitivity are more fully described in &#8220;Asset/Liability Management&#8221; under &#8220;Item 1. Business&#8221; and &#8220;Asset/Liability Management and Market Risk&#8221; under &#8220;Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosure About Market Risk&#8221;.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Legislative and regulatory actions taken now or in the future may significantly affect BKFC&#8217;s financial condition, results of operations, liquidity or stock price.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There have been numerous actions undertaken in Congress, the Treasury Department, the FRB, the FDIC, the SEC and others in an effort to address the recent liquidity and credit crisis in the financial industry that followed the sub-prime mortgage market meltdown, which began in late 2007. These measures include the TARP CPP (under which the Treasury Department&#8217;s authority to make new investments expired on October 3, 2010); homeowner relief that encourages loan restructuring and modification; the establishment of significant liquidity and credit facilities for financial institutions and investment banks; the lowering of the federal funds rate; emergency action against short selling practices; a temporary guaranty program for money market funds; the establishment of a commercial paper funding facility to provide back-stop liquidity to commercial paper issuers; a mandatory &#8220;stress test&#8221; requirement for banking institutions with assets in excess of $100 billion to analyze capital sufficiency and risk exposure; and coordinated international efforts to address illiquidity and other weaknesses in the banking sector. The purpose of these legislative and regulatory actions was to help stabilize the U.S. banking system. However, these and any current or future legislative or regulatory initiatives may not have their desired effect, or may have an adverse effect when applied to BKFC.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The most recent of these actions was the passage into law on July 21, 2010 of the Dodd-Frank Act.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Dodd-Frank Act represents a significant overhaul of many aspects of the regulation of the financial-services industry, addressing, among other things, systemic risk, capital adequacy, deposit insurance assessments, consumer financial protection, interchange fees, derivatives, lending limits, and changes among the bank regulatory agencies.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Many of these provisions are subject to further study, rulemaking and to the discretion of regulatory bodies.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">While many of the provisions in the Dodd-Frank Act are aimed at financial institutions that are significantly larger than BKFC or the Bank, there are provisions with which we will have to comply now that the Dodd-Frank Act has become law.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For instance, we will be subject to a new assessment model from the FDIC based on assets, not deposits, and be subject to enhanced executive compensation and corporate governance requirements. Because many aspects of this legislation remain subject to ongoing agency rulemaking, including public comment periods prior to implementation, it is difficult to predict at this time the complete extent of the effects that the Dodd-Frank Act will have on us.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As rules and regulations are promulgated by the federal agencies responsible for implementing and enforcing the provisions in the Dodd-Frank Act, we will have to work to apply resources to ensure that we are in compliance with all applicable provisions, which may adversely impact our earnings. Furthermore, any current or future legislative or regulatory initiatives may not have their desired effect, or may have an adverse effect when applied to us.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Failure to meet any of the various capital adequacy guidelines which we are subject to could adversely affect our operations and could compromise the status of BKFC as a bank holding company.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BKFC and the Bank are required to meet certain regulatory capital adequacy guidelines and other regulatory requirements imposed by the FRB, the FDIC and the Department. If BKFC or the Bank fails to meet these minimum capital guidelines and other regulatory requirements, our financial condition and results of operations would be materially and adversely affected and could compromise the status of BKFC as a banking holding company. See &#8220;Regulatory Capital Requirements&#8221; under &#8220;Item 1. Business&#8221; for detailed capital guidelines for bank holding companies and banks.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Non-compliance with applicable laws and/or regulations, including the Bank Secrecy Act and USA Patriot Act, may adversely affect BKFC&#8217;s operations and financial results and could result in significant fines or sanctions.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></I></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 15pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Federal and state regulators have the ability to impose substantial sanctions, restrictions and requirements on the Bank if they determine, upon examination or otherwise, that we have violated laws or regulations with which we must comply, or that weaknesses or failures exist with respect to general standards of safety and soundness.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such enforcement may be formal or informal and can include, among other things, orders to take certain actions or to refrain from certain actions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The imposition of regulatory sanctions may have adverse effects on BKFC, including a material impact on its financial condition.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, compliance with any such action could distract management&#8217;s attention from operations, cause significant expenses, restrict BKFC from engaging in potentially profitable activities, and limit BKFC&#8217;s ability to raise capital.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 15pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 15pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The USA Patriot and Bank Secrecy Acts require financial institutions to develop programs to prevent the institutions from being used for money laundering and terrorist activities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If certain activities are detected, financial institutions are obligated to file suspicious activity reports with the Treasury Department&#8217;s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These rules also require financial institutions to establish procedures for identifying and verifying the identity of customers seeking to open new financial accounts or conduct transactions, and require the filing of certain reports, such as those for cash transactions above a certain threshold.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Financial institutions must also refrain from transacting business with certain countries or persons designated by the Office of Foreign Assets Control.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 15pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 15pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Non-compliance with laws and regulations such as these could result in significant fines or sanctions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These particular laws and regulations have significant implications for all financial institutions, establish new crimes and penalties, and require the federal banking agencies, in reviewing merger and acquisition transactions, to consider the effectiveness of the parties to such transactions in combating money laundering and terrorist activities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Even inadvertent non-compliance and technical failure to follow the regulations may result in significant fines or other penalties, which could have a material adverse impact on BKFC&#8217;s business, financial condition, results of operations or liquidity.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 15pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The value of the securities in our investment securities portfolio may be negatively affected by continued disruptions in securities markets.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Due to heightened credit and liquidity risks and the volatile economy, making the determination of the value of a securities portfolio is less certain.&#160; There can be no assurance that decline in market value associated with these disruptions will not result in other-than-temporary or permanent impairments of these assets, which would lead to accounting charges which could have a material negative effect on our financial condition and results of operations.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank could be held responsible for environmental liabilities relating to properties acquired through foreclosure, resulting in significant financial loss.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the event the Bank forecloses on a defaulted commercial or residential mortgage loan to recover its investment, it may be subject to environmental liabilities in connection with the underlying real property, which could significantly exceed the value of the real property.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Although the Bank exercises due diligence to discover potential environmental liabilities prior to acquiring any property through foreclosure, hazardous substances or wastes, contaminants, pollutants or their sources may be discovered on properties during its ownership or after a sale to a third party.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BKFC cannot assure you that the Bank would not incur full recourse liability for the entire cost of any removal and cleanup on an acquired property, that the cost of removal and cleanup would not exceed the value of the property or that the Bank could recover any of the costs from any third party.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Losses arising from environmental liabilities could have a material adverse impact on BKFC&#8217;s business, financial condition, results of operations or liquidity.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BKFC is subject to liquidity risk, which could disrupt our ability to meet our financial obligations.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Liquidity refers to the ability of BKFC to ensure sufficient levels of cash to fund operations, such as meeting deposit withdrawals, funding loan commitments, paying expenses and meeting quarterly payment obligations under certain subordinated debentures issued by BKFC in connection with the issuance of floating rate redeemable trust preferred securities issued by BKFC&#8217;s unconsolidated trust subsidiary. The source of the funds for BKFC&#8217;s debt obligations is dependent on the Bank. If needed, the Bank has the ability to borrow term and overnight funds from the FHLB or other financial intermediaries. The Bank also has $341 million of securities designated as available-for-sale that can serve as sources of funds as of December 31, 2013. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">While management is satisfied that BKFC&#8217;s liquidity is sufficient at December 31, 2013 to meet known and potential obligations, any significant restriction or disruption of BKFC&#8217;s ability to obtain funding from these or other sources could have a negative effect on BKFC&#8217;s ability to satisfy its current and future financial obligations, which could materially affect BKFC&#8217;s financial condition.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BKFC is a bank holding company, and its sources of funds are limited.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BKFC is a bank holding company and its operations are primarily conducted by the Bank, which is subject to significant federal and state regulation. Cash available to pay dividends to shareholders of BKFC is derived primarily from dividends paid by the Bank. As a result, BKFC&#8217;s ability to receive dividends or loans from its subsidiaries is restricted. Under federal law, the payment of dividends by the Bank is subject to capital adequacy requirements. The FRB and/or the FDIC prohibit a dividend payment by BKFC or the Bank that would constitute an unsafe or unsound practice. See &#8220;Dividend Restrictions&#8221; under &#8220;Item 1. Business&#8221;.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The inability of the Bank to generate profits and pay such dividends to BKFC, or regulator restrictions on the payment of such dividends to BKFC even if earned, would have an adverse effect on the financial condition and results of operations of BKFC and BKFC&#8217;s ability to pay dividends to its shareholders.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, since BKFC is a legal entity separate and distinct from the Bank, its right to participate in the distribution of assets of the Bank upon the Bank&#8217;s liquidation, reorganization or otherwise will be subject to the prior claims of the Bank&#8217;s creditors, which will generally take priority over the Bank&#8217;s shareholders.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our Common Stock price can be volatile.</FONT></B></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 24.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our Common Stock price can fluctuate widely in response to a variety of factors, making it more difficult for you to resell your Common Stock at prices you find attractive and at the time you want. Factors include actual or anticipated variations in our quarterly operating results; changes in recommendations or projections by securities analysts; operating and stock price performance of other companies deemed to be peers; news reports and perception in the marketplace regarding BKFC, our competitors and/or the financial services industry as a whole; results of litigation; significant acquisitions or business combinations involving BKFC or our competitors; and other factors, including those described in this &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; section.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>

  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BKFC regularly explores opportunities to acquire financial services businesses or assets and may also consider opportunities to acquire other banks or financial institutions. In 2007, we acquired FNB Bancorporation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In 2009, we acquired certain banking offices and assumed certain deposit liabilities of Integra Bank, as well as adding the investment professionals of TAM to the Bank&#8217;s trust department.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In 2011, we completed the purchase of one banking office of United Kentucky Bank in Falmouth, Kentucky and a portfolio of selected loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Difficulty in integrating an acquired business or company such as those described above or other businesses we acquire in the future may cause BKFC not to realize expected revenue increases, cost savings, increases in geographic or product presence, and/or other projected benefits. The integration could result in higher than expected customer deposit attrition (run-off), loss of key employees, disruption of BKFC&#8217;s business or the business of the acquired company, or otherwise adversely affect BKFC&#8217;s ability to maintain relationships with customers and employees or achieve the anticipated benefits of the acquisition. Also, the negative effect of any divestitures required by regulatory authorities in acquisitions or business combinations may be greater than expected.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Certain provisions of BKFC&#8217;s articles of incorporation and bylaws may make it more difficult to acquire control of BKFC by means of a tender offer, open market purchase, proxy fight or otherwise.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For example, the articles require the affirmative vote of a majority of the outstanding voting power of BKFC or, if the Board of Directors recommends against the approval of certain matters, by the holders of at least 75% of the voting power to, among other things, adopt (i) an amendment to the articles or bylaws, (ii) an agreement of merger or consolidation, (iii) a proposed combination or majority share acquisition involving the issuance of shares of BKFC and requiring shareholder approval, and (iv) a proposal to sell, exchange, transfer or otherwise dispose of all, or substantially all, of BKFC&#8217;s assets.</FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Higher FDIC deposit insurance premiums and assessments could adversely impact our earnings.</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 22.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FDIC insurance rates increased significantly in 2009, and we may pay higher FDIC premiums in the future.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Dodd-Frank Act established 1.35% as the minimum DRR. The FDIC has determined that the DRR should be 2.0% and has adopted a plan under which it will meet the statutory minimum DRR of 1.35% by the statutory deadline of September&#160;30, 2020. The Dodd-Frank Act requires the FDIC to offset the effect on institutions with assets less than $10 billion of the increase in the statutory minimum DRR to 1.35% from the former statutory minimum of 1.15%, although the FDIC has not announced how it will implement this offset.</FONT></DIV>

It is possible that our insurance premiums will increase under these regulations.</FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We rely on other companies to provide key components of our business infrastructure.</FONT></B></DIV>

  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Third parties provide key components of our business infrastructure such as banking services, processing, and Internet connections.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Any disruption in such services provided by these third parties or any failure of these third parties to handle current or higher volumes of use could adversely affect our ability to deliver products and services to clients and otherwise to conduct business.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Technological difficulties of a third party service provider could adversely affect our business to the extent those difficulties result in the interruption of services provided by that party.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A cyber security breach of a vendor&#8217;s system may result in theft of our data or disruption of business processes.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A material breach of customer data security at a service provider&#8217;s site may negatively impact our business reputation and cause a loss of customers; result in increased expense and may result in litigation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We rely on our outsourced service providers to implement and maintain prudent cyber security controls.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Furthermore, we may not be insured against all types of losses as a result of third party failures and our insurance coverage may be inadequate to cover all losses resulting from system failures or other disruptions.</FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Holders and Dividends</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>There were 7,619,999 shares of Common Stock outstanding on December 31, 2013, which were held of record by 773 shareholders.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Board of Directors declared cash dividends of $0.18 per share in December 2013, $0.17 per share in September 2013, $0.17 per share in June 2013, $0.17 per share in March 2013. The dividends declared in December 2012 were paid in January of 2013 in connection with BKFC&#8217;s decision to pay dividends on a quarterly basis starting in 2013. BKFC paid dividends on a semi-annual basis in 2011 and 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>In 2012, the Board of Directors declared cash dividends of $0.30 per share in February 2012, $0.32 per share in August 2012 and<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>$0.17 per share in December 2012<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">OVERVIEW</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The business of BKFC consists of holding and administering its interest in the Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank conducts basic banking operations from locations in Boone, Kenton, Campbell, Grant, Gallatin and Pendelton Counties in northern Kentucky and Hamilton County in Ohio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The majority of BKFC&#8217;s revenue is derived from the Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The loan portfolio is diversified and the ability of borrowers to repay their loans is not dependent upon any single industry.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The majority of the Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio, approximately 77%, consists of loans secured by or with real estate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans secured by or with real estate are further categorized down by loan type and borrower.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Included in loans secured with or by real estate as of December 31, 2013 are residential real estate loans, commercial real estate loans and owner-occupied commercial real estate loans.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U></U>&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Economic Overview</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The year ended December 31, 2013 saw slow growth both nationally and in the geographic markets where we operate.&#160; The United States&#8217; gross domestic product (GDP) improved each of the first three quarters of 2013 before decreasing slightly in the fourth-quarter.&#160; For the full year 2013, the economy experienced year-over-year growth of 1.9%.&#160; While the economy continues to show improvement, the rate of growth remains well below a historical normalized rate of 3%.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Overall economic growth was further sustained by increased consumer spending, which grew at rate of 2.3% for 2013, which exceeded the rate of growth for both 2011 and 2012.&#160; Unemployment declined, beginning at 8% and ending at 6.7% in 2013.&#160; <FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">However, the percent of eligible workforce employed is well below historical averages.</FONT>&#160; Home values rose slightly and equities, despite much uncertainty, finished the year with substantial gains.&#160; <U></U></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Regulatory Reform Developments</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On July 21, 2010, President Obama signed the Dodd-Frank Act into law. The Dodd-Frank Act is intended to address perceived deficiencies and gaps in the regulatory framework for financial services in the United States, reduce the risks of bank failures and better equip the nation&#8217;s regulators to guard against or mitigate any future financial crises, and manage systemic risk through increased supervision of systemically important financial companies (including nonbank financial companies). The Dodd-Frank Act implements numerous and far-reaching changes across the financial landscape affecting financial companies, including banks and bank holding companies such as BKFC.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For a review of the various changes that the Dodd-Frank Act implements, see &#8220;Regulation and Supervision &#151; The Dodd-Frank Act&#8221; in &#8220;Item 1. Business&#8221; of this Annual Report.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Many of the rulemakings required by the various regulatory agencies are still in the process of being developed and/or implemented.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2013 Performance Overview</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2013, BKFC was able to achieve strong operating results in a challenging banking environment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>The challenges faced in 2013 included slow loan growth, compressing net interest margins and increased cost associated with regulatory compliance.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Despite these challenges, overall improving credit metrics, accompanied with increased fee revenue and controlled overhead expenses resulted in a 9% increase in net income in 2013 compared with 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The provision for loan losses decreased 33%, and non-interest income increased 7%, which offset an increase in non-interest expense of 1% and a decrease in net interest income of 2% in 2013 compared with 2012.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Although slower than the pre-recession levels, BKFC&#8217;s growth in average loans outstanding in 2013 was the highest organic loan growth experienced since 2008.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Total average loans outstanding increased $51 million, or 4.5%, in 2013 compared with 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
<B>  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%">
    <TR>  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="left">
</TD>
  <TD
style="FONT-STYLE: normal; WIDTH: 34%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" align="center">
35</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="right">
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD><BR /></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;BACKGROUND-COLOR: rgb(0,0,0); FONT-STYLE: normal; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
</B>  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As discussed above, management believes that BKFC has benefited from the 2013 improvements in the economy.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This is demonstrated in the improving credit metrics compared with 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Net charge-offs decreased from $8,720,000 in 2012 to $4,962,000 in 2013 and non-performing loans decreased from $19,283,000 at the end of 2012 to $15,438,000 at the end of 2013.</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">These improving credit quality metrics led the Bank to provide $4,700,000 in the provision for loans losses in 2013 compared to $7,000,000 in 2012. While net charge-offs and non-performing loans both decreased in 2013, they remained at a historically high level.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">While the economy continued to show signs of improvement during 2013, BKFC continued to experience levels of defaults and foreclosures higher than historical levels during fiscal 2013, but lower than 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such default levels have been significantly less compared with other regions of the country.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This is due, in part, to the fact that BKFC&#8217;s market in northern Kentucky and Cincinnati did not experience as dramatic a rise in real estate values<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>in the years preceding the last recession compared with other markets, such as Florida and California.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>While BKFC&#8217;s local markets have not been affected as severely as other markets, management continues to closely monitor developments in the real estate market, given that the majority of the Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio is real estate related.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">While the level of resources devoted to the credit review function and working out problem loans continued to be high in 2013, BKFC did not make significant changes to its loan underwriting standards.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BKFC&#8217;s willingness to make loans to qualified applicants that meet its traditional, prudent lending standards has not changed.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">While BKFC benefited from the slow recovery and the improving credit metrics compared with 2012, management does not foresee a return to pre-recession levels of credit metrics in the near future.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Despite the recovery, high unemployment and low real estate values continued to place significant economic strain on a majority of the Bank&#8217;s business partners. The Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio has been most significantly affected by economic conditions.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following sections provide more detail on subjects presented in this overview.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CRITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BKFC has prepared all of the consolidated financial information in this quarterly report in accordance with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In preparing the consolidated financial statements in accordance with GAAP, BKFC makes estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amount of assets and liabilities, disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements, and the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the reporting period.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>There can be no assurances that actual results will not differ from those estimates.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have identified the accounting policy related to the allowance for loan losses as critical to the understanding of BKFC&#8217;s results of operations, since the application of this policy requires significant management assumptions and estimates that could result in reporting materially different amounts if conditions or underlying circumstances were to change.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank maintains an allowance to absorb probable, incurred loan losses inherent in the loan portfolio. The Bank&#8217;s policy is to maintain an allowance for loan losses at an adequate level based upon ongoing quarterly assessments and evaluations of the collectability and historical loss experience of loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loan losses are charged and recoveries are credited to the allowance for loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Provisions for loan losses are based on the Bank&#8217;s review of its historical loan loss experience and such factors that, in management&#8217;s judgment, deserve consideration under existing economic conditions in estimating probable loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank&#8217;s strategy for credit risk management includes a combination of well-defined credit policies, uniform underwriting criteria, and ongoing risk monitoring and review processes for all commercial and consumer credit exposures.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The credit risk management strategy also includes assessments of compliance with commercial and consumer policies, risk ratings and other important credit information.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The strategy also emphasizes regular credit examinations and management reviews of loans exhibiting deterioration in credit quality.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank strives to identify potential problem loans early and promptly undertake the appropriate actions necessary to mitigate or eliminate the increasing risk identified in these loans.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt;">  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%">
    <TR>  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="left">
</TD>
  <TD
style="FONT-STYLE: normal; WIDTH: 34%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" align="center">
36</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="right">
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD><BR /></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 2px solid; FONT-STYLE: normal; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
</font></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The allowance for loan losses consists of two components, the specific reserve, pursuant to ASC 310, <I>Accounting by Creditors for Impairment of a Loan</I>, and the general reserve, pursuant to ASC 450-10, <I>Accounting for Contingencies</I>.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A loan is considered impaired when, based upon current information and events, it is probable that the Bank will be unable to collect all amounts due according to the contractual terms of the loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The specific reserve component is an estimate of loss based upon an impairment review of<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>loans which meet certain criteria that are considered impaired. An insignificant delay or insignificant shortfall in amount of payments is not considered an impairment. In addition, a loan is not impaired during a period of delay in payment if the creditor expects to collect all amounts due including interest accrued at the contractual interest rate for the period of delay.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Thus, a demand loan or loan that has been extended beyond its original maturity date is not impaired if the creditor expects to collect all amounts due including interest accrued at the contractual interest rate during the period the loan is outstanding.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The general reserve includes an estimate of commercial and consumer loans with similar characteristics. Depending on the set of facts with respect to a particular loan, the Bank utilizes one of the following methods for determining the proper impairment of a loan:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <TABLE
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0pt; TABLE-LAYOUT: fixed; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; dtth: tableHanging" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
    <TR
style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 0pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; PADDING-TOP: 0in">
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0.25in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0.25in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Symbol; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#183;</FONT></FONT></TD>
  <TD
style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">the present value of expected future cash flows of a loan;</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <TABLE
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0pt; TABLE-LAYOUT: fixed; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; dtth: tableHanging" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
    <TR
style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 0pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; PADDING-TOP: 0in">
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0.25in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0.25in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Symbol; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#183;</FONT></FONT></TD>
  <TD
style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">the market price of the loan based upon readily available information for that type of loan; and</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <TABLE
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0pt; TABLE-LAYOUT: fixed; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; dtth: tableHanging" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
    <TR
style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 0pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; PADDING-TOP: 0in">
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0.25in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0.25in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Symbol; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#183;</FONT></FONT></TD>
  <TD
style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">the fair value of collateral.</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The allowance established for impaired loans is generally based, for all collateral-dependent loans, on the fair value of the collateral, less the estimated cost to liquidate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For non-collateral dependent loans (such as accruing troubled debt restructurings), the allowance is based on the present value of expected future cash flows discounted by the loan&#8217;s effective interest rate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A small portion of the Bank&#8217;s loans which are impaired under the ASC 310 process carry no specific reserve allocation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loans were reviewed for impairment and are considered adequately collateralized with respect to their respective outstanding principal loan balances.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The majority of these loans are loans which have had their respective impairment (or specific reserve) amounts charged off, or are loans related to other impaired loans which continue to have a specific reserve allocation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It is the Bank&#8217;s practice to maintain these impaired loans, as analyzed and provided for in the ASC 310 component of the allowance for loan losses, to avoid double counting of any estimated losses that may have been included in the ASC 450-10 component of the allowance for loan losses. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Generally, the Bank orders a new or updated appraisal on real estate properties which are subject to an impairment review.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Upon completion of the impairment review, loan reserves are increased as warranted.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Charge-offs, if necessary, are generally recognized in a period after the reserves were established. Adjustments to new or updated appraisal values are not typically done, but in those cases when an adjustment is necessary, it is documented with supporting information and typically results in an adjustment to decrease the property&#8217;s value because of additional information obtained concerning the property after the appraisal or update has been received by the Bank. The Bank&#8217;s practice is to obtain new or updated appraisals or evaluation on the loans subject to impairment. If a new or updated appraisal is not available at the time of a loan&#8217;s impairment review, the Bank typically applies a discount to the value of an old appraisal to reflect the property&#8217;s current estimated value if there is believed to be deterioration in either (i) the physical or economic aspects of the subject property or (ii) any market conditions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Updated valuations on 1 to 4 family residential properties with small to moderate values are generally accomplished by obtaining an evaluation or appraisal.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Generally, an &#8220;as is&#8221; value is utilized in most of the Bank&#8217;s real estate based impairment analyses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, under certain limited circumstances, an &#8220;as stabilized&#8221; valuation may be utilized, provided that the &#8220;as stabilized&#8221; value is tied to a well-justified action plan to bring the real estate project to a stabilized occupancy under a reasonable period of time.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">If a partially charged-off loan has been restructured in a manner that is reasonably assured of repayment and performance according to prudently modified terms, and has sustained historical payment performance for a reasonable period of time prior to and/or after the restructuring, it may be returned to accrual status and is classified as a TDR loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, if the above conditions cannot be reasonably met, the loan remains on non-accrual status.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, the Bank evaluates the collectability of both principal and interest when assessing the need for loans to be placed on non-accrual status. Non-accrual status denotes loans in which, in the opinion of management, the collection of additional interest is unlikely. A loan is generally placed on non-accrual status if: (i) it becomes 90 days or more past due or (ii) for which payment in full of both principal and interest cannot be reasonably expected.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%">
    <TR>  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="left">
</TD>
  <TD
style="FONT-STYLE: normal; WIDTH: 34%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" align="center">
37</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="right">
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD><BR /></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;BACKGROUND-COLOR: rgb(0,0,0); FONT-STYLE: normal; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The general component of the allowance covers non-impaired loans and is based on historical loss experience adjusted for current factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For loans that are risk rated, the historical loss experience is determined based on the actual loss history experienced by the Company over the most recent 4 years.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loss ratios are calculated from a migration analysis of the charge offs over this period,<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>but excludes the ratios from the most recent twelve month period as they are not appropriately seasoned. The loss ratios for loans designated as belonging to homogeneous pools, including smaller balance consumer loans, are calculated for a five year period and a one year period, with the higher of the two loss ratio&#8217;s currently used in the allowance calculation. These actual loss experiences are supplemented with other economic factors based on the risks present for each portfolio segment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These economic factors include consideration of the following:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>levels of and trends in delinquencies and impaired loans; trends in volume and terms of loans;<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>other changes in lending policies, procedures, and practices; experience, ability, and depth of lending management and other relevant staff; national and local economic trends and conditions; industry conditions; and effects of changes in credit concentrations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These factors are consistent within each of the portfolio segments, which have been identified as:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>commercial, residential real estate, nonresidential real estate, construction, consumer and municipal obligations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management utilizes a detailed approach to setting the environmental adjustments to the historical loss.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Factors that management considers as part of this approach in setting the environmental adjustments include economic trends, loan policies, lender experience, loan growth, delinquency trend, non-performing asset trends, classified loan trends and credit concentrations.&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Reserves on individual loans and historical loss rates are reviewed quarterly and adjusted as necessary based on changing borrower and/or collateral conditions, as well as actual collection and charge-off experience.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Charge-offs are recognized when it becomes evident that a loan or a portion of a loan is deemed uncollectible regardless of its delinquent status.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank generally charges off that portion of a loan that is determined to be unsupported by an obligor&#8217;s continued ability to repay the loan from income and/or assets, both pledged and unpledged as collateral.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FINANCIAL CONDITION</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Highlighting the changes to the BKFC balance sheet from December 31, 2012 to December 31, 2013 was loan growth.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>Total loans increased $54,236,000, or 4.5%, from the end of 2012 to the end of 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Total deposits increased $17,578,000, or 1%, from the end of 2012 to the end of 2013, while total short-term borrowings decreased $13,765,000, or 33%, in the same period.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Total capital increased $10,699,000, or 6%, from the end of 2012 to the end of 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The increase in capital was a result of an increase in retained earnings, which was partially offset by a decrease in accumulated other comprehensive income of $5,704,000 and the $2,151,000 repurchase of the Warrant issued in connection with the CPP Program.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The decrease in the comprehensive income was the result of decline in the market value of BKFC&#8217;s available-for-sale security portfolio. The value of the securities portfolio declined as rates moved higher in 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Warrant permitted the Treasury to purchase 276,078.12 shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock at an exercise price of $18.473 per share. As a result of these changes, the Bank&#8217;s total assets increased $13,388,000, or 1%, from $1,844,104,000 at December 31, 2012 to $1,857,492,000 at December 31, 2013. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other changes on the asset side of the balance sheet included a $26,679,000, or 8%, increase in available-for-sale securities, a $10,167,000, or 15%, increase in held-to-maturity securities, and a $5,998,000, or 18%, increase in company owned life insurance, which was partially offset by $13,110,000, or 80%, decrease in loans held for sale.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The increase in company owned life insurance was the result of $5,000,000 in new policies purchased in the first quarter of 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The decrease in loans held for sale was a result of the lower levels of mortgage loan refinancing activity, brought on by higher long term interest rates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The largest increases in loans came from the commercial portfolio, which increased $40,410,000, or 20%, and the municipal obligations portfolio which increased $12,930,000, or 56%, from the end of 2012 to the end of 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management of the Bank was encouraged by the increase in loan demand experienced in 2013 and intends to continue to make loans that meet its longstanding prudent lending standards.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The largest increase in deposits came from interest-bearing transaction NOW accounts, which increased $61,666,000, or 12%, from 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Contributing to the increase in NOW accounts was public fund deposits which increased $48,717,000 or 13% from 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The increase in NOW accounts were partially offset by a $58,227,000, or 16%, decrease in certificates of deposit (CDs) from the end of 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management believes that the lower level of interest rates offered on CDs have made them less desirable to consumers.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Summary</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></I></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2013 vs. 2012</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Driven by lower loan loss provisions and increased non-interest income, net income increased 9% from $18,145,000 for the year ended December 31, 2012, to $19,765,000 for the year ended December 31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The provision for loan losses decreased $2,300,000 from $7,000,000 in 2012 to $4,700,000 in 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The decrease in the provision reflected the overall improved credit metrics and slowly improving economic conditions compared with 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These metrics included net charge-offs that decreased from $8,720,000 (0.77% of average loans) in 2012 to $4,962,000 (0.42% of average loans) in 2013, <FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">decreased criticized and classified loans by 5%,</FONT> and non-performing loans that decreased 20% from $19,283,000 at December 31, 2012 to $15,438,000 at December 31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Total non-interest income increased $1,590,000, or 7%, from $22,421,000 in 2012 to $24,011,000 in 2013, as higher service charges on deposits and trust income offset lower sold loan income. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></I></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2012 vs. 2011</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Driven by lower loan loss provisions and lower preferred stock dividends, net income available to common shareholders increased 17% from $15,517,000 for the year ended December 31, 2011, to $18,145,000 for the year ended December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The provision for loan losses decreased $3,750,000 from $10,750,000 in 2011 to $7,000,000 in 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The decrease in the provision reflected the overall improved<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>credit metrics and slowly improving economic conditions compared with 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These metrics included net charge-offs that decreased from $9,830,000 (0.88% of average loans) in 2011 to $8,720,000 (0.77% of average loans) in 2012, and criticized and classified loans that decreased 17% from $106,838,000 at December 31, 2011 to $88,263,000 at December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Total preferred stock dividends and discount accretion, which are not tax deductible, decreased $972,000, or 100%, from $972,000 in 2011 to nil in 2012 as a result of the TARP CPP repurchases in 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The operating results also included a $4,224,000, or 10%, increase in non-interest expense which was partially offset by an increase in revenue of $2,344,000, or 2%.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>

</DIV>
</B>  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Net Interest Income</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></I></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2013 vs. 2012</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Net interest income dropped to $55,254,000 in 2013, a decrease of $931,000 (2%) from the $56,185,000 earned in 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As illustrated in <U>Table 3</U>, while the volume variance had a positive impact on net interest income, the rate variances had a negative impact on net interest income in 2013 in contrast to 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT><U>Table 3</U> shows the net interest income on a fully tax equivalent basis was positively impacted by the volume additions to the balance sheet by $2,913,000, which was offset by a negative rate variance by $4,016,000. As illustrated in <U>Table 2</U>, the net interest spread decreased by 16 basis points and the net interest margin of 3.44% for 2013 was 18 basis points lower than the 3.62% net interest margin for 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Contributing to the decrease in both of these measures was the current extreme low rate environment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The cost of interest-bearing liabilities decreased 14 basis points from 0.50% for 2012 to 0.36% for 2013, while the yield on earning assets decreased 30 basis points from 4.02% for 2012 to 3.72% for 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As illustrated in <U>Table 2</U>, average earning assets increased $54,095,000, or 3%, from 2012 to 2013, while average interest-bearing liabilities only increased $14,492,000, or 1%, in the same period.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As further illustrated in <U>Table 3</U>, the unfavorable rate variance was driven by the decrease in interest income attributable to rate of $5,385,000 while the decrease in interest expense attributable to rate was only $1,369,000.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT>Driving the decrease in interest income were loans, which contributed $4,984,000 or 93% of the decrease in interest income as a result of rate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BKFC is expected to be negatively affected if rates continue to fall in 2014.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For more information on the Bank&#8217;s interest rate risk, see the section entitled &#8220;Asset/Liability Management and Market Risk&#8221; under &#8220;Item 7A.&#8221;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></I></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2012 vs. 2011</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Net interest income grew to $56,185,000 in 2012, an increase of $647,000 (1%) over the $55,538,000 earned in 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As illustrated in <U>Table 3</U>, while the volume variance had a positive impact on net interest income, the rate variances had a negative impact on net interest income in 2012 in contrast to 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT><U>Table 3</U> shows the net interest income on a fully tax equivalent basis was positively impacted by the volume additions to the balance sheet by $2,628,000, which was partially offset by a negative rate variance by $1,818,000. As illustrated in <U>Table 2</U>, the net interest spread decreased by 7 basis points and the net interest margin of 3.62% for 2012 was 11 basis points lower than the 3.73% net interest margin for 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Contributing to the decrease in both of these measures was the current extreme low rate environment and the change in the mix of average assets as discussed above in the financial condition section of this Annual Report.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The cost of interest-bearing liabilities decreased 25 basis points from 0.75% for 2011 to 0.50% for 2012, while the yield on earning assets decreased 32 basis points from 4.34% for 2011 to 4.02% for 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As illustrated in <U>Table 2</U>, average earning assets increased $68,493,000, or 5%, from 2011 to 2012, while average interest-bearing liabilities only increased $42,316,000, or 3%, in the same period.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As further illustrated in <U>Table 3</U>, the unfavorable rate variance was driven by the decrease in interest income attributable to rate of $4,459,000 while the decrease in interest expense attributable to rate was only $2,641,000.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT>Driving the decrease in interest income were loans, which contributed $3,588,000 or 80% of the decrease in interest income as a result of rate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BKFC is expected to be negatively affected if rates continue to fall in 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For more information on the Bank&#8217;s interest rate risk, see the section entitled &#8220;Asset/Liability Management and Market Risk&#8221; under &#8220;Item 7A.&#8221;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></I></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Average Yield</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT><U>Table 2</U>, shown below, illustrates the Bank&#8217;s average balance sheet information and reflects the average yield on interest-earning assets, on a tax equivalent basis, and the average cost of interest-bearing liabilities for the periods indicated.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such yields and costs are derived by dividing income or expense by the average monthly balance of interest-earning assets or interest-bearing liabilities, respectively, for the years presented.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Average balances are daily averages for the Bank and include non-accruing loans in the loan portfolio, net of the allowance for loan losses.</FONT></DIV>

<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Volume/Rate Analysis</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT><U>Table 3</U> below illustrates the extent to which changes in interest rates and changes in volume of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities have affected the Bank&#8217;s interest income and expense during the periods indicated.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For each category of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, information is provided on changes attributable to: (i) changes in volume (change in volume multiplied by prior year rate); (ii) changes in rate (change in rate multiplied by prior year volume); and (iii) a combination of changes in rate and volume.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The combined effects of changes in both volume and rate, which cannot be separately identified, have been allocated proportionately to the change due to volume and the change due to rate.</FONT></DIV>
