<SUP><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(1)</FONT></SUP><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT>Includes short-term investments and interest-bearing deposits in other financial institutions.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U></U>&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Provision for loan losses</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">- Like many other financial institutions, the Bank has been significantly affected by the most recent national economic recession and the continued challenging economic environment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>While the Bank experienced an increase in defaults and foreclosures since the recession began, the levels of such activity has been significantly less than other regions in the country due, in part, to the fact that the Bank&#8217;s market in the Northern Kentucky and Greater Cincinnati area did not experience as dramatic a rise in real estate values over the years preceding this recession, as other markets had.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management believes that with the continuing economic uncertainty, high unemployment rates and low real estate values, the resulting pressure on earnings will remain above historical levels.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">While the economic conditions continue to be challenging, the provision for loan losses reflected the improving economy that was discussed above in the economic overview.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>While still above historical levels, the credit metrics showed<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>improvement in 2013 compared with 2012. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></I></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2013 vs. 2012</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As discussed above under &#8220;Management Overview,&#8221; the provision for loan losses reflected the slow economic recovery.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The provision for loan losses was $4,700,000 for the year ended December 31, 2013, compared to $7,000,000 for 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As detailed in <U>Table 4</U>, the decrease of $2,300,000 (33%) reflected a decrease in the level of charge-offs, non-performing loans and lower specific reserves in 2013 compared with 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For the year ended December 31, 2013, net charge-offs were $4,962,000, or 0.42%, of average loan balances compared to $8,720,000, or 0.77%, of average loan balances, for 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Non-performing loans decreased 20% from $19,283,000 at December 31, 2012 to $15,438,000 at December 31, 2013, while criticized and classified loans decrease by 5% and specific loan reserves decreased 50% from $6,265,000 to $3,419,000 over the same period. </FONT></DIV>

  <DIV

<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2012 vs. 2011</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As discussed above under &#8220;Management Overview,&#8221; the provision for loan losses reflected the slow economic recovery.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The provision for loan losses was $7,000,000 for the year ended December 31, 2012, compared to $10,750,000 for 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The decrease of $3,750,000 (35%) reflected a decrease in the level of charge-offs, criticized and classified loans and lower specific reserves in 2012 compared with 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For the year ended December 31, 2012, net charge-offs were $8,720,000, or 0.77%, of average loan balances compared to $9,830,000, or 0.88%, of average loan balances, for 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Criticized and classified loans decreased 17% from $106,838,000 at December 31, 2011 to $88,263,000 at December 31, 2012, and specific loan reserves decreased 16% from $7,433,000 to $6,265,000 over the same period. </FONT></DIV>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT>As illustrated in <U>Table 5</U> below, total non-accrual loans plus accruing loans past due 90 days or more were $19,283,000 (1.61% of loans outstanding) at December 31, 2012, compared to $15,870,000 (1.40% of loans outstanding) at December 31, 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>Contributing to the increase in non-performing loans from December 31, 2011 to December 31, 2012 was one commercial relationship which added approximately $7,000,000 to non-accruing loans in the fourth quarter of 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This relationship was reported as an accruing restructured loan in December of 2011. Management&#8217;s evaluation of the inherent risk in the loan portfolio considers both historical losses and information regarding specific borrowers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management continues to monitor the non-performing relationships and has established appropriate reserves.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Non-performing assets, which include non-performing loans and other real estate owned, totaled $24,679,000 at December 31, 2012 and $21,714,000 at December 31, 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This represented 1.34% of total assets at December 31, 2012 compared to 1.25% at December 31, 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>While non-performing loans increased in 2012, other real estate owned decreased from $5,844,000 at December 31, 2011 to $5,396,000 at December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These properties are recorded at their fair value less estimated costs to sell with the difference between this value and the loan balance being recorded as a charge-off.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></I></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Troubled Debt Restructurings (TDRs)</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In certain circumstances, the Bank may modify the terms of a loan to maximize the collection of amounts due.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In cases where the borrower is experiencing financial difficulties or is expected to experience difficulties in the near -term, concessionary modification is granted to minimize or eliminate the economic loss and to avoid foreclosure or repossession of the collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Modifications may include interest rate reductions, extension of the maturity date or a reduction in the principal balance.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Restructured loans accrue interest as long as the borrower complies with the modified terms.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Performing TDRs are loans that are paying as to the agreed upon modified terms and are not more than 30 days past due.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Non performing TDRs are the remainder. Total performing TDRs, which are not considered non-performing loans by management, were $8,816,000 at December 31, 2013 compared with $6,046,000 at December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Total non-performing TDRs were $8,246,000 at December 31, 2013 compared with $11,095,000 at December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In order to proactively manage and resolve problem loans, the Bank expects higher than normal levels of TDRs as it continues to work with relationships that show signs of stress.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>All TDRs are considered impaired loans and any specific reserves related to the TDRs are included in the allowance for loan losses on the balance sheet.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Any additional specific reserves related to TDRs added or reduced in a period would be reflected in the provision for loan losses on the income statement for that period.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Ordinarily, loans are identified as potential problem loans, through a higher risk weighting, before actually being restructured.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>

style="WIDTH: 100%">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;BACKGROUND-COLOR: rgb(0,0,0); FONT-STYLE: normal; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Allowance for Loan Losses (&#8220;ALL&#8221;)</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The decrease in the ALL was directionally consistent in 2013 with the improving credit metrics and the slow economic recovery.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The ALL decreased 2%, from $16,568,000 at December 31, 2012 to $16,306,000 at December 31, 2013, which decreased the allowance for loan losses as a percentage of total loans from 1.39% at December 31, 2012, to 1.30% at December 31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amount of the allowance allocated to impaired loans at year end 2013 was $3,419,000, which was down 50% from the $6,265,000 at year end 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amount of the allowance allocated to specific pools of loans based on risk ratings increased in 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This increase was a result of a higher volume of substandard loans which did not have specific allocations, from the end of 2013 to the end of 2012. The impairment process is described in the critical accounting policies section of this Annual Report.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>While the allowance decreased in 2013, it has increased significantly since the recession began in 2008. Contributing to the increase in the allowance for loan losses over this period is the significant decrease in real estate values experienced in the current economic cycle. Management believes the current level of the ALL is sufficient to absorb probable incurred losses in the loan portfolio. Management continues to monitor the loan portfolio closely and believes the provision for loan losses is directionally consistent with the changes in the probable losses inherent in the loan portfolio from 2012 to 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank does not originate or purchase sub-prime loans for its portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management will continue to monitor and evaluate the effects of the<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>housing market conditions and any signs of further deterioration in credit quality on the Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management believes the current economic strains will continue into 2014 and expects continuing higher than normal credit losses and provisioning expense in the foreseeable future.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Monitoring loan quality and maintaining an adequate allowance is an ongoing process overseen by senior management and the loan review function.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On at least a quarterly basis, a formal analysis of the adequacy of the ALL is prepared and reviewed by management and the Board of Directors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This analysis serves as a point in time assessment of the level of the ALL and serves as a basis for provisions for loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The loan quality monitoring process includes assigning loan grades and the use of a watch list to identify loans of concern. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For additional information on the ALL, see the critical accounting policies section of this discussion.</FONT></DIV>

Total non-interest income increased $1,590,000, or 7%, as higher service charges and fees,<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>trust fee income, bankcard transaction revenue more than offset lower mortgage banking income and higher losses on the sale of other real estate owned property.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The $1,234,000, or 14%, increase in service charges and fees was driven by a new fee structure put in place in the second quarter of 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The $1,128,000, or 40%, decrease in mortgage banking income was driven by an increase in long-term interest rates in 2013, which prompted a decrease in demand for home mortgage loan refinancing.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Driving the $560,000, or 20%, increase was higher assets under management and increased sales of brokerage products.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The $723,000, or 24%, increase in other non-interest income included $413,000 higher loan fees in 2013 compared with 2012, the majority of which was fees earned for facilitating interest rate swaps for customers. <FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Dodd-Frank Act excludes banks under $10 billion in assets from the rule that limits the interchange fees paid by merchants<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> </FONT>to banks for certain debit card transactions.</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></I></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2012 vs. 2011</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">. Total non-interest income increased $1,697,000, or 8%, as higher mortgage banking income, bankcard transaction revenue, trust fee income, and company owned life insurance earnings more than offset lower service charges and fees on deposits and higher losses on the sale of other real estate owned property.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The $997,000, or 56%, increase in mortgage banking income was driven by a sharp drop in long-term interest rates in 2012, which prompted an increase in demand for home mortgage loan refinancing.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Driving the $352,000, or 4%, decrease in service charges was the lower overdraft fees.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The $385,000, or 11%, increase in bankcard transaction revenue reflected consumers&#8217; continued acceptance of electronic forms of payment and the resulting growth in usage of the Bank&#8217;s debit and credit card products.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Dodd-Frank Act excludes banks under $10 billion in assets from the rule that limits the interchange fees paid by merchants<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>to banks for certain debit card transactions. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT>2013 vs. 2012.</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Non-interest expense increased $407,000 (1%), to $46,745,000 for 2013, compared to $46,338,000 for 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The largest increase in non-interest expense was in the salaries and benefits expense, which increased $608,000 (3%) in 2013 compared to 2012. The increase in salaries and benefits included $286,000 in higher accruals for pension plan expense.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The increased pension plan expense was the result of higher projected earnings for plan participants.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The largest decrease in other non-interest expense was appraisal expense, which decreased $207,000 (47%) in 2013 compared with 2012, as the result of a decrease in the number of<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>loans sold.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2012 vs. 2011.</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Non-interest expense increased $4,224,000 (10%), to $46,338,000 for 2012, compared to $42,114,000 for 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>The largest increase in non-interest expense was in the salaries and benefits expense, which increased $2,759,000 (14%) in 2012 compared to 2011. The increase in salaries and benefits included $556,000 in higher accruals for bonuses, $451,000 in higher incentive expense and $335,000 in higher accruals for pension plan expense.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The added bonus accrual reflects the end of the TARP restriction on bonus pay for executives, while the increased pension plan expense was the result of a lower discount rate applied to future benefits.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The increase in incentive cost was related to the higher mortgage banking income.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The largest decrease in non-interest expense was FDIC insurance expense, which decreased $378,000 (25%) in 2012 compared with 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank benefited from the provision of the Dodd-Frank Act that changed the base on which the insurance is calculated from total deposits to total assets.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Tax Expense</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></I></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2013 vs. 2012</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As a result of higher income before taxes, the federal income tax expense increased $932,000 (13%) to $8,055,000 for 2013 compared to $7,123,000 for 2012. The effective tax rate was 29.0% for 2013, an increase of .8% from 28.2% for 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The increase in effective tax rate was a result of a lower ratio of tax exempt income and tax credit investments to income before taxes<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>in 2013 compared with 2012. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></I></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2012 vs. 2011</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As a result of higher income before taxes, the federal income tax expense increased $214,000 (3%) to $7,123,000 for 2012 compared to $6,909,000 for 2011. The effective tax rate was 28.2% for 2012,<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>a decrease of 1.3% from 29.5% for 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The decrease in effective tax rate was a result of increased tax exempt income and an additional tax credit investment, which reduced taxes by $299,000 in 2012 compared with 2011. </FONT></DIV>

  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Unused lines of credit and loan commitments assure a borrower of financing for a specified period of time at a specified rate. The risk to the Bank under such commitments is limited to the terms of the contracts.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For example, the Bank may not be obligated to advance funds if the customer&#8217;s financial condition deteriorates or if the customer fails to meet specific covenants. An approved, but unfunded, loan commitment represents a potential credit risk once the funds are advanced to the customer. The unused lines of credit and loan commitments also represent a future cash requirement, but this cash requirement will be limited since many commitments are expected to expire or only be used partially.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Standby letters of credit represent commitments by the Bank to repay a third-party beneficiary when a customer fails to repay a loan or debt instrument. The terms and risk of loss involved in issuing standby letters of credit are similar to those involved in issuing loan commitments and extending credit.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition to credit risk, the letters of credit could present an immediate cash requirement if the obligations require funding. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank maintains letters of credit from the FHLB to collateralize public funds deposits.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These letters of credit reduce the Bank&#8217;s available borrowing line at the FHLB.</FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Liquidity and Capital Resources</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Liquidity refers to the availability of sufficient levels of cash to fund BKFC&#8217;s operations, such as meeting deposit withdrawals, funding loan commitments, paying expenses, meeting its quarterly payment obligations under certain subordinated debentures issued by BKFC in connection with the issuance of floating rate redeemable trust preferred securities issued by BKFC&#8217;s unconsolidated trust subsidiary.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The source of the funds for BKFC&#8217;s debt obligations is dependent on the Bank. During 2013, as discussed in the financial condition section of this Annual Report, the growth in securities and loans were funded by the growth in deposits and the reduction of short-term investments. At December 31, 2013, the Bank&#8217;s customers had available $455,571,000 in unused lines and letters of credit, and the Bank has further extended loan commitments totaling $15,697,000.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Historically, many such commitments have expired without being drawn and, accordingly, do not necessarily represent future cash commitments.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2009 BKFC filed a universal shelf registration statement on Form S-3 that was declared effective in November, 2010.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This registration statement permits BKFC to engage in offerings of up to $50 million aggregate principal amount of debt securities, common stock, preferred stock, purchase contracts, units, warrants, rights and any combination of the foregoing.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BKFC utilized the shelf registration to offer Common Stock in connection with the $28.1 million common Stock offering completed in November, 2010.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As of the date of this Annual Report the 2009 shelf registration statement has expired.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We may elect to utilize future registration statements that we may file with the SEC, to conduct subsequent registered debt or equity offerings.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">If needed, the Bank has the ability to borrow term and overnight funds from the FHLB or other financial intermediaries.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Further, the Bank also has $341,123,000 of securities designated as available-for-sale and an additional $3,828,000 of held-to-maturity securities that mature within one year that can serve as sources of funds.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management is satisfied that BKFC&#8217;s liquidity is sufficient at December 31, 2013 to meet known and potential obligations.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As illustrated in BKFC&#8217;s statement of cash flows, the net change in cash and cash equivalents from 2013 compared with 2012 was a decrease of $73,211,000.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Net income provided $19,765,000 of the $44,451,000 in the Bank&#8217;s cash flows from operating activities, while the largest cash outflow from investing activities was in the form of an increase in loans of $63,701,000.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As discussed in the financial condition section of this Annual Report, the largest source of cash from financing activities came from the increase in deposits.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The FDIC has issued regulations relating a bank&#8217;s deposit insurance assessment and certain aspects of its operations to specified capital levels.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A &#8220;well-capitalized&#8221; bank, one with a leverage ratio of 5% or more and a Total Risk-Based Ratio of 10% or more, and no particular areas of supervisory concern, pays the lowest premium and is subject to the fewest restrictions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank&#8217;s capital levels and ratios exceed the regulatory definitions of well-capitalized institutions. At December 31, 2013, BKFC&#8217;s Leverage Ratio and Total Risk-Based Ratios were 9.61% and&#160;13.37%, respectively, which exceed all required ratios established for bank holding companies. </FONT></DIV>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effect of Inflation and Changing Prices</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The financial statements and related financial data presented in this Annual Report have been prepared in accordance with GAAP, which require the measurement of financial position and operating results in terms of historical dollars without considering the change in the relative purchasing power of money over time due to inflation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The primary impact of inflation on our operations is reflected in increased operating costs.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Unlike most industrial companies, virtually all the assets and liabilities of a financial institution are monetary in nature.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As a result, interest rates generally have a more significant impact on a financial institution&#8217;s performance than do general levels of inflation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Interest rates do not necessarily move in the same direction or to the same extent as the prices of goods and&#160;services.</FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">

  <DIV

<B></B>&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In July 2013, the FASB amended existing guidance relating to testing indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amendment permits an assessment of qualitative factors to determine whether the existence of events and circumstances indicates that it is more likely than not that the indefinite-lived intangible asset is impaired.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If, after assessing the totality of events and circumstances, it is concluded that it is not more likely than not that the indefinite-lived intangible asset is impaired, then no further action is required.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, after the same assessment, if it is concluded that it is more like than not that the indefinite-lived intangible asset is impaired, then a quantitative impairment test should be performed whereby the fair value of the indefinite-lived intangible asset is compared to the carrying amount.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amendments in this guidance are effective for annual and interim impairment tests performed for fiscal years beginning after September 15, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Early adoption is permitted.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The effect of adopting this standard did not have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s operating results or financial condition. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In February 2013, the FASB amended existing guidance related to reporting amounts reclassified out of other comprehensive income out of accumulated other comprehensive income.&#160; These amendments do not change the current requirements for reporting net income or other comprehensive income in financial statements. These amendments require an entity to provide information about the amounts reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income by component. In addition, an entity is required to present, either on the face of the statement where net income is presented or in the notes, significant amounts reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income by the respective line items of net income but only if the amount reclassified is required under U.S. GAAP to be reclassified to net income in its entirety in the same reporting period. For other amounts that are not required under U.S. GAAP to be reclassified in their entirety to net income, an entity is required to cross-reference to other disclosures required under U.S. GAAP that provide additional details about those amounts.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The effect of adopting this standard did not have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s operating results or financial condition. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B>Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosure About Market Risk</B></FONT></DIV>
<BR />  <DIV  name="SectionRPT37201420057PM"
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both;clear:both;">
</DIV>
  <div
style="clear:both">
</div>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Asset/Liability Management and Market Risk</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Market risk is the risk of loss arising from adverse changes in the fair value of financial instruments due to interest rate risk, exchange rate risk, equity price risk or commodity price risk.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank does not maintain a trading account for any class of financial instrument and is not currently subject to foreign currency exchange rate risk, equity price risk or commodity price risk.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank&#8217;s market risk is composed primarily of interest rate risk. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%">
    <TR>  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="left">
</TD>
  <TD
style="FONT-STYLE: normal; WIDTH: 34%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" align="center">
50</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="right">
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD><BR /></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;BACKGROUND-COLOR: rgb(0,0,0); FONT-STYLE: normal; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank utilizes an earnings simulation model to measure and define the amount of interest rate risk it assumes.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Interest rate risk is the potential for economic losses due to future interest rate changes. These economic losses can be reflected as a loss of future net interest income and/or a decline in fair market values. Interest rate risk results from the fact that the interest sensitive assets and liabilities can adjust their rates at different times and by different amounts.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The goal of asset/liability management is to maintain a high, yet stable, net interest margin and to manage the effect that changes in market interest rates will have on net interest income.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A common measure of interest rate risk is interest rate &#8220;gap&#8221; measurement.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The gap is the difference, in dollars, between the amount of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities that will reprice within a certain time frame.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Repricing can occur when an asset or liability matures or, if an adjustable rate instrument, when it can be adjusted.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Typically, the measurement will focus on the interest rate gap position over the next 12 months.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>An institution is said to have a negative gap position when more interest-bearing liabilities reprice within a certain period than interest-earning assets, and a positive gap position when more interest-earning assets reprice than interest-bearing liabilities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Interest rate gap is considered an indicator of the effect that changing rates may have on net interest income.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Generally, an institution with a negative gap will benefit from declining market interest rates and be negatively impacted by rising interest rates. The Bank currently is in a negative gap position, $266,251,000 (14.33%), and as a result would, without considering other factors, generally benefit from lower rates and be negatively impacted by higher interest rates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The ability to benefit from the Bank&#8217;s liability-sensitive position would depend on a number of factors, including: the competitive pressures on consumer deposit and loan pricing; the movement of certain deposit rate indices in relationship to asset rate indices; and the extent of the decrease in the rate environment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2013, BKFC&#8217;s 12-month interest rate gap position, as measured by the Bank&#8217;s asset/liability model, was negative.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Over the preceding 12 months, interest rate sensitive liabilities exceeded interest rate sensitive assets by $266,251,000 (14.33% of total assets).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2012, interest rate sensitive liabilities exceeded interest rate sensitive assets by $123,737,000 (6.71% of total assets).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank&#8217;s asset/liability management policy establishes guidelines governing the amount of interest income at risk, market value at risk and parameters for the gap position. Management continually monitors these risks through the use of gap analysis and the earnings simulation model.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The simulation model is used to estimate and evaluate the impact of changing interest rates on earnings and market value.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The model projects the effect of instantaneous movements in interest rates of both 100 and 200 basis points.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The assumptions used in the simulation are inherently uncertain and, as a result, the model cannot precisely measure future net interest income.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The results of the model are used by management to approximate the results of rate changes and do not indicate actual expected results. Actual results will differ from the model&#8217;s simulated results due to timing, frequency of interest rate changes as well as changes in various management strategies and market conditions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Additionally, actual results can differ materially from the model if interest rates do not move equally across the yield curve.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The changes in the estimates of an increasing rate scenario on the net interest income change, as shown below, from 2012 to 2013 were a result of the same influences that increased the liability sensitivity of BKFC&#8217;s gap position and show that risk to income from rate changes would be negative in a rising rate environment. Although the gap position is negative, or in a liability sensitive position, the results of the simulation show income would also decline in a falling rate environment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The effects of the estimates for a decreasing rate environment are the results of the current rate environment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In December of 2008, the FRB lowered the targeted federal funds rate to 0.25%, and as a result most short-term deposit interest rates cannot drop 100 basis points while earning assets could in theory decrease by these amounts. The result of this extreme low rate environment is a declining rate scenario which produces a negative impact on earnings.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Board of Directors and Shareholders</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank of Kentucky Financial Corporation</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Crestview Hills, Kentucky</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of The Bank of Kentucky Financial Corporation as of December&#160;31, 2013 and 2012 and the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, changes in shareholders&#8217; equity, and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December&#160;31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We also have audited The Bank of Kentucky Financial Corporation&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2013, based on criteria established in the 1992<I> Internal Control &#150; Integrated Framework </I>issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank of Kentucky Financial Corporation&#8217;s management is responsible for these financial statements, for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting included in Item 9A.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements and an opinion on the company's internal control over financial reporting based on our audits.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Those standards require that we plan and perform the audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement and whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Our audits of the financial statements included examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, and evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Our audit of internal control over financial reporting included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Our audits also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinions.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A company's internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A company's internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company's assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Basis of Presentation</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of The Bank of Kentucky Financial Corporation (the Company) and its wholly owned subsidiary, The Bank of Kentucky (the Bank).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Intercompany transactions are eliminated in consolidation.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Description of Business</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company provides financial services through its subsidiary, which operates primarily in Boone, Campbell, Grant, Gallatin, Kenton and Pendleton counties in northern Kentucky and also in Greater Cincinnati, Ohio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Operations consist of generating commercial, mortgage and consumer loans and accepting deposits from customers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The loan portfolio is diversified and the ability of debtors to repay loans is not dependent upon any single industry.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The majority of the institution&#8217;s loans are secured by specific items of collateral including business assets, real property and consumer assets.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Use of Estimates</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>To prepare financial statements in conformity with U.S. generally accepted principles, management makes estimates and assumptions based on available information.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These estimates and assumptions affect the amounts reported in the financial statements and the disclosures provided, and future results could differ.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The allowance for loan losses and the fair values of financial instruments are particularly subject to change.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Cash Flows</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Cash and cash equivalents include cash on hand, amounts due from banks, and federal funds sold.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company reports net cash flows for customer loan and deposit transactions, interest-bearing balances with banks,<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>short-term borrowings with maturities of 90 days or less, and property and equipment.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Interest-Bearing Deposits in Other Financial Institutions</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Interest-bearing deposits in other financial institutions mature within one year and are carried at cost.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Securities</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Securities are classified as held-to-maturity and carried at amortized cost when management has the positive intent and ability to hold them to maturity.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Securities are classified as available-for-sale when they might be sold before maturity.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Available-for-sale securities are carried at fair value, with unrealized holding gains and losses reported in other comprehensive income, net of tax.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Interest income includes amortization of purchase premium or discount.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Premiums and discounts on securities are amortized on the level-yield method without anticipating prepayments except for mortgage backed securities where prepayments are anticipated.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Gains and losses on sales are based on the amortized cost of the security sold.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management evaluates securities for other-than-temporary impairment (&#8220;OTTI&#8221;) at least on a quarterly basis, and more frequently when economic or market conditions warrant such an evaluation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In determining OTTI, management considers many factors, including: (1) the length of time and the extent to which the fair value has been less than cost, (2) the financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer, (3) whether the market decline was affected by macroeconomic conditions, and (4) whether the Company has the intent to sell the debt security or more likely than not will be required to sell the debt security before its anticipated recovery.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The assessment of whether an other-than temporary decline exists involves a high degree of subjectivity and judgment and is based on the information available to management at a point in time.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"  align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>

    <TR>  <TD

  <DIV

</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #f0f0f0; BORDER-LEFT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #f0f0f0; BORDER-RIGHT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-TOP: 0in"  valign="top" width="100%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"  align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #f0f0f0; BORDER-LEFT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #f0f0f0; BORDER-RIGHT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-TOP: 0in"  valign="top" width="100%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"  align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: #f0f0f0; BORDER-LEFT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #f0f0f0; BORDER-RIGHT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-TOP: 0in"  valign="top" width="100%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"  align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Dollar amounts in thousands, except per share amounts)</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: windowtext 1pt solid; BORDER-LEFT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #f0f0f0; BORDER-RIGHT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-TOP: 0in"  valign="top" width="100%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"  align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">When OTTI occurs, the amount of the OTTI recognized in earnings depends on whether the Company intends to sell the security or more likely than not will be required to sell the security before recovery of its amortized cost basis less any current-period credit loss.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If the Company intends to sell or more likely than not will be required to sell the security before recovery of its amortized cost basis less any current-period credit loss, the OTTI shall be recognized in earnings equal to the entire difference between the investment&#8217;s amortized cost basis and its fair value at the balance sheet date.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Otherwise, the OTTI shall be separated into the amount representing the credit loss and the amount related to all other factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amount of the total OTTI related to the credit loss is determined based on the present value of cash flows expected to be collected and is recognized in earnings.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amount of the total OTTI related to other factors shall be recognized in other comprehensive income, net of applicable taxes.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The previous amortized cost basis less the OTTI recognized in earnings shall become the new amortized cost basis of the investment.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans Held For Sale</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank originates loans for sale to secondary market brokers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans held for sale are loans which have been closed and are awaiting delivery to these brokers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>They are reported at the lower of cost or fair value, on an aggregate basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Net unrealized losses, if any, are recorded as a valuation allowance and charged to earnings.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Most loans are sold servicing released such that there would be no servicing asset recognized upon the sale.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans that management has the intent and ability to hold for the foreseeable future or until maturity or payoff are reported at the principal balance outstanding, purchase premiums and discounts, deferred loan fees and costs, and an allowance for loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Interest income is accrued on the unpaid principal balance.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loan origination fees, net of certain direct origination costs, are deferred and recognized in interest income using the level-yield method without anticipating prepayments.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Interest income on mortgage, consumer&#160;and commercial loans is discontinued at the time the loan is 90 days delinquent unless the loan is well-secured and in process of collection.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Interest income is not reported when full loan repayment is in doubt, typically when the loan is impaired or payments are significantly past due.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Past due status is based on the contractual terms of the loan.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">All interest accrued but not received for loans placed on nonaccrual is reversed against interest income.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Interest received on such loans is accounted for on cost-recovery method, until qualifying for return to accrual.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans are returned to accrual status when all the principal and interest amounts contractually due are brought current and future payments are reasonably assured.<U></U></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Troubled debt restructurings (TDR&#8217;s) are separately identified for impairment disclosures and are measured at the present value of estimated future cash flows using the loan&#8217;s effective rate at inception.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If a troubled debt restructuring is considered to be a collateral dependent loan, the loan is reported, net, at the fair value of the collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For troubled debt restructurings that subsequently default, the Company determines the amount of reserve in accordance with the accounting policy for the allowance for loan losses.<U></U></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"  align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV>&#160;</DIV>

&#160;   <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In general, once a modified loan is considered a TDR, the loan will always be considered a TDR, and therefore impaired, until it is paid in full, otherwise settled, sold or charged off.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, the Company&#8217;s policy also permits for loans to be removed from TDR status in the years following the restructuring if the following two conditions are met: (1) the restructuring agreement specifies an interest rate equal to or greater than the rate that the Company was willing to accept at the time of the restructuring for a new loan with comparable risk, and (2) the loan is performing in accordance with its restructured terms.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>To determine if the interest rate is a market rate, management will look at the interest rates on the Bank&#8217;s pool of similar risk graded credits.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management will also consider other financial and non-financial factors to determine if a loan can be removed from TDR status.<U></U></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.75in; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">If a partially charged-off loan has been restructured in a manner that is reasonably assured of repayment and performance according to prudently modified terms, and has sustained historical payment performance for a reasonable period of time of at least six months prior to and/or after the restructuring, it may be returned to accrual status and classified as a TDR loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, in limited situations, the Company may restore the accrual status of a TDR loan under a shorter period of time (versus the aforementioned minimum six month post-restructuring payment performance), if the restructuring coincides with another event which substantially improves a borrower&#8217;s financial condition and ability to repay the restructured loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such an event might include substantial new leases in a troubled real estate project, significant new sources of business revenues (i.e. new contracts) or significant new equity contributed from a source not financed by the Company.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company also performs a financial analysis to determine the borrower&#8217;s current capacity to repay the loan, as modified before it is returned to accrual status.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, if the above conditions cannot be reasonably met, the loan remains on non-accrual status.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Concentration of Credit Risk:</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Most of the Company&#8217;s business activity is with customers located within Northern Kentucky and the Cincinnati metropolitan area.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Therefore, the Company&#8217;s exposure to credit risk is significantly affected by changes in the economy in this area.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="COLOR: #4f81bd; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Allowance for Loan Losses</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The allowance for loan losses is a valuation allowance for probable incurred credit losses, increased by the provision for loan losses and decreased by charge-offs less recoveries.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management estimates the allowance balance required using past loan loss experience, the nature and volume of the portfolio, information about specific borrower situations and estimated collateral values, economic conditions, and other factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Allocations of the allowance may be made for specific loans, but the entire allowance is available for any loan that, in management&#8217;s judgment, should be charged off.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loan losses are charged against the allowance when management believes the uncollectibility of a loan balance is confirmed.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The allowance consists of specific and general components.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The specific component relates to loans that are individually classified as impaired.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The general component covers both classified and non-classified loans and is based on historical loss experience adjusted for current factors.&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"  align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>

  <TR>  <TD

  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The general component covers non-impaired loans and is based on historical loss experience adjusted for current factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For loans that are risk rated, the historical loss experience is determined based on the actual loss history experienced by the Company over the most recent 4 years.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loss ratios are calculated from a migration analysis of the charge offs over this period,<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>but excludes the ratios from the most recent twelve month period as they are not appropriately seasoned.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In 2013 the migration analysis was adjusted from excluding the most recent six month period to the current twelve month period.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This change was the result of management&#8217;s determination that the results of the loss ratios calculated using the six month period were unrealistically low, and therefore reduced the loss ratios to a level that management felt were too low.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management believes that this change gives a better reflection of the probable incurred losses in the non-impaired loans and this adjustment makes the ratios less volatile.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>The loss ratios for loans designated as belonging to homogeneous pools, including smaller balance consumer loans, are calculated for a five year period and a one year period, with the higher of the two loss ratios currently used in the allowance calculation. These actual loss experiences are supplemented with other economic factors based on the risks present for each portfolio segment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These economic factors include consideration of the following:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>levels of and trends in delinquencies and impaired loans; trends in volume and terms of loans;<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>other changes in lending policies, procedures, and practices; experience, ability, and depth of lending management and other relevant staff; national and local economic trends and conditions; industry conditions; and effects of changes in credit concentrations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These factors are consistent within each of the portfolio segments, which have been identified as:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>commercial, residential real estate, nonresidential real estate, construction, consumer and municipal obligations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The risk characteristics of each of the identified portfolio segments are as follows:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Commercial</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: Commercial loans are primarily based on the identified cash flows of the borrower and secondarily on the underlying collateral provided by the borrower.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Borrowers may be subject to adverse economic conditions that can lead to decreases in product demand; increasing material or other production costs; interest rate increases that could have an adverse impact on profitability; non-payment of credit that has been extended under normal vendor terms for goods sold or services extended; and interruption related to the importing or exporting of production materials or sold products.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Residential Real Estate</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Residential real estate loans are secured by 1-4 family residences and are generally owner occupied; the Company generally establishes a maximum loan-to-value ratio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Home equity loans are typically secured by a subordinate interest in 1-4 family residences.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loans are subject to adverse employment conditions in the local economy leading to increased default rate; decreased market values from oversupply in a geographic area and; impact to borrowers&#8217; ability to maintain payments in the event of incremental rate increases on adjustable rate mortgages.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Non Residential Real Estate</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Nonresidential real estate loans are viewed primarily as cash flow loans and secondarily as loans secured by real estate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Commercial real estate lending typically involves higher loan principal amounts and the repayment of these loans is generally dependent on the successful operation of the property securing the loan or the business conducted on the property securing the loan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loans are subject to adverse market conditions that cause a decrease in market value or lease rates and; the potential for environmental impairment and the obsolescence of the location or function.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Construction</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Construction loans are underwritten utilizing independent appraisal reviews, absorption rate analysis, lease rates and financial analysis of the developers and property owners.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Construction loans are generally based on estimates of costs and value associated with the complete project.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loans are subject to adverse market conditions that cause a decrease in market value or absorption rates and; the potential for environmental impairment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loans are closely monitored by on-site inspections and are considered to have higher risks than other real estate loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
