</TR>
  <TR>  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: windowtext 1pt solid; BORDER-LEFT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #f0f0f0; BORDER-RIGHT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="100%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Consumer</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Consumer loans generally consist of loans secured by personal property or unsecured loans such as credit cards.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Repayment of these loans is primarily dependent on the personal income of the borrowers, who are subject to adverse employment conditions in the local economy which may lead to higher unemployment.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Municipal Obligations</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>Municipal obligations are generally secured by specific assets or the taxing power of the municipality.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loans are subject to adverse employment conditions in the local economy and lower real estate values which can reduce the municipality&#8217;s tax base. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A loan is impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that the Company will be unable to collect all amounts due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans, for which the terms have been modified resulting in a concession, and for which the borrower is experiencing financial difficulties, are considered troubled debt restructurings and classified as impaired. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Impairment is evaluated in total for smaller-balance loans of similar nature such as residential mortgage, consumer, and credit card loans, and on an individual loan basis for other loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Large groups of smaller balance homogeneous loans, such as consumer and residential real estate loans, are collectively evaluated for impairment, and accordingly, they are not separately identified for impairment disclosures.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If a loan is impaired, a portion of the allowance is allocated so that the loan is reported, net, at the present value of estimated future cash flows using the loan&#8217;s existing rate or at the fair value of collateral if repayment is expected solely from the collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Troubled debt restructurings are separately identified for impairment disclosures and are measured at the present value of estimated future cash flows using the loan&#8217;s effective rate at inception.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If a troubled debt restructuring is considered to be a collateral dependent loan, the loan is reported, net, at the fair value of the collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For troubled debt restructurings that subsequently default, the Company determines the amount of reserve in accordance with the accounting policy for the allowance for loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company&#8217;s impairment policies are consistent across all of the loan portfolio segments. Recorded investment excludes accrued interest, due to materiality. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Premises and Equipment</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Land is carried at cost.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Premises and equipment are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Buildings and related components are depreciated using the straight-line method with useful lives ranging from <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">10</FONT> to <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">25</FONT> years.&#160;<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT>Leasehold improvements are depreciated using the straight-line method over the lesser of the useful life of the asset or the length of the lease.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Furniture, fixtures and equipment are depreciated using the straight-line method with useful lives ranging from <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3</FONT> to <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">10</FONT> years.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Transfers of Financial Assets</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Transfers of financial assets are accounted for as sales, when control over the assets has been relinquished.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Control over transferred assets is deemed to be surrendered when the assets have been isolated from the Company, the transferee obtains the right (free of conditions that constrain it from taking advantage of that right) to pledge or exchange the transferred assets, and the Company does not maintain effective control over the transferred assets through an agreement to repurchase them before their maturity.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other Real Estate</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Other real estate acquired through or instead of foreclosure is initially recorded at fair value less cost to sell when acquired, establishing a new cost basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If fair value declines subsequent to foreclosure, a valuation allowance is recorded through expense.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Expenses incurred in carrying other real estate are charged to operations as incurred.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A total of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">5,305</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">5,396</FONT> of other real estate was owned on December 31, 2013 and 2012, respectively, and included in other assets.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"  align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV>&#160;</DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) Stock</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank is a member of the FHLB system.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Members are required to own a certain amount of stock based on the level of borrowings and other factors, and may invest in additional amounts.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>FHLB stock is carried at cost, classified as a restricted security, and periodically evaluated for impairment based on ultimate recovery of par value.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Both cash and stock dividends are reported as income.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Company Owned Life Insurance</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company has purchased life insurance policies on certain key executives.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Company owned life insurance is recorded at the amount that can be realized under the insurance contract at the balance sheet date, which is the cash surrender value adjusted for other charges or other amounts due that are probable at settlement.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</FONT></U><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Goodwill resulting from business combinations prior to January 1, 2009 represents the excess of the purchase price over the fair value of the net assets of businesses acquired.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Goodwill resulting from business combinations after January 1, 2009 is generally determined as the excess of the fair value of the consideration transferred plus the fair value of any non-controlling interests in the acquiree, over the fair value of the net assets acquired and liabilities assumed as of the acquisition date.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Goodwill and intangible assets acquired in a purchase business combination and determined to have an indefinite useful life are not amortized, but tested for impairment at least annually, or more frequently if events and circumstances exist that indicate that a goodwill impairment test should be performed.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company has selected December 31 as the date to perform the annual impairment test.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Intangible assets with definite useful lives are amortized over their estimated useful lives to their estimated residual values.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Goodwill is the only intangible asset with an indefinite life on our balance sheet.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other intangible assets consist of core deposit and acquired customer relationship intangible assets arising from whole bank, branch and asset management business acquisitions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>They are initially measured at fair value and then are amortized on an accelerated method over their estimated useful lives of four to ten years. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Prepaid FDIC Insurance</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On September 29, 2009, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) adopted an Amended Restoration Plan to allow the Deposit Insurance Fund to return to a reserve ratio of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.15</FONT>% within eight years, as mandated by statute.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As part of the Amended Restoration Plan, the FDIC amended its assessment regulations to require all institutions to prepay on December 30, 2009 their estimated risk-based insurance assessments for the fourth quarter of 2009, and for all of 2010, 2011, and 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At that same time, institutions were also required to pay their regular quarterly assessments for the third quarter of 2009.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The prepaid assessment amount was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">0</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,848</FONT> on December 30, 2013 and 2012, and is included in other assets. <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT>On July 1, 2013, the FDIC returned $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,159</FONT> to the Bank as the Restoration Plan came to an end and FDIC assessments are now paid quarterly.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Repurchase Agreements</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Substantially all repurchase agreement liabilities represent amounts advanced by various customers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Securities are pledged to cover these liabilities, which are not covered by federal deposit insurance.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Stock-Based Compensation</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Compensation cost is recognized for stock options and restricted stock units issued to directors and officers, based on the fair value of these awards at the date of grant.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For stock options, a Black-Scholes model is utilized to estimate the fair value of stock options.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For restricted stocks units the fair value is equal to the stock price on the day the units are granted.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Compensation cost is recognized over the required service period, generally defined as the vesting period.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For awards with graded vesting, compensation cost is recognized on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period for the entire award. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Income Taxes</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: Income tax expense is the amount of taxes payable for the current year plus or minus the change in deferred taxes.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Deferred tax liabilities and assets are the expected future tax consequences of temporary differences between the carrying amounts and tax bases of assets and liabilities, computed using enacted tax rates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Recognition of deferred tax assets is limited by the establishment of a valuation allowance unless management concludes that they are more likely than not to result in future tax benefits to the Company.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A tax position is recognized as a benefit only if it is &#8220;more likely than not&#8221; that the tax position would be sustained in a tax examination, with a tax examination being presumed to occur.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amount recognized is the largest amount of tax benefit that is greater than 50% likely of being realized on examination.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For tax positions not meeting the &#8220;more likely than not&#8221; test, no tax benefit is recorded.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company recognizes interest and/or penalties related to income tax matters in income tax expense.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loan Commitments and Related Financial Instruments</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Financial instruments include credit instruments, such as commitments to make loans and standby letters of credit, issued to meet customer financing needs.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The face amount of these items represents the exposure to loss, before considering customer collateral or ability to repay.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such financial instruments are recorded when they are funded.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Instruments, such as standby letters of credit that are considered financial guarantees are recorded at fair value.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Fair Value of Financial Instruments</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Fair values of financial instruments are estimated using relevant market information and other assumptions, as more fully disclosed in a separate note.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Fair value estimates involve uncertainties and matters of significant judgment regarding interest rates, credit risk, prepayments and other factors, especially in the absence of broad markets for particular items.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Changes in assumptions or in market conditions could significantly affect the estimates.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loss Contingencies</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loss contingencies, including claims and legal actions arising in the ordinary course of business, are recorded as liabilities when the likelihood of loss is probable and an amount or range of loss can be reasonably estimated.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management does not believe there are currently such matters that will have a material effect on the financial statements.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Comprehensive Income</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Comprehensive income consists of net income and other comprehensive income (loss).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Other comprehensive income (loss) includes unrealized gains and losses on securities available for sale which are also recognized as separate components of equity. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Dividend Restriction</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Banking regulations require the maintenance of certain capital levels and may limit the amount of dividends which may be paid by the Bank to the Company or by the Company to its shareholders.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>See Note 16 for further discussion.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"  align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Long-term Assets</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These assets are reviewed for impairment when events indicate their carrying amount may not be recoverable from future undiscounted cash flows.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If impaired, the assets are recorded at fair value.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Restrictions on Cash</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Cash on hand or on deposit with the Federal Reserve Bank was required to meet regulatory reserve and clearing requirements.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Business Segment</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Internal financial information is reported and aggregated in one line of business, banking.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>While the chief decision-makers monitor the revenue streams of the various products and services, the identifiable segments are not material and operations are managed and financial performance is evaluated on a Company-wide basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Accordingly, all of the financial service operations are considered by management to be aggregated in one reportable operating segment.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Reclassifications</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Some items in the prior year financial statements were reclassified to conform to the current presentation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Reclassifications had no material effect on the financial statements.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Derivative Financial Instruments</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank operates an interest rate protection program in which the Bank earns a fee by providing the Bank&#8217;s commercial loan customers the ability to swap from variable to fixed, or fixed to variable interest rates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under these agreements the Bank enters into a variable or fixed rate loan agreement with its customer in addition to a swap agreement.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The swap agreement effectively swaps the customer&#8217;s variable rate to a fixed rate or vice versa.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank then enters into a corresponding swap agreement with a third party in order to swap its exposure on the variable to fixed rate swap with the Bank&#8217;s customer.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The agreements are considered standalone derivatives and changes in the fair value of derivatives are reported in earnings as noninterest income<B>.</B></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank is exposed to losses if a counterparty fails to make its payments under a contract in which the Bank is in the receiving status.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In this situation the Bank receives collateral from the counterparty for the fair market value of the derivative.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Also, the Bank minimizes its credit risk by monitoring the credit standing of the counterparties.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We anticipate the counterparties will be able to fully satisfy their obligations under these agreements.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Earnings Per Common Share</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Basic earnings per common share is net income available to common shareholders divided by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Diluted earnings per common share includes the dilutive effect of additional potential common shares issuable under stock options, restricted stock units, and warrants.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Earnings and dividends per share are restated for all stock splits and stock dividends through the date of issuance of the financial statements.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Retirement Plans</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Employee 401(k) and profit sharing plan expense is the amount of matching contributions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Deferred compensation and supplemental retirement plan expense allocates the benefits over years of service.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><U>Trust Fee Income</U>: Income is accounted for on an accrual basis.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Adoption of New Accounting Standards</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In July 2013, the FASB amended existing guidance relating to testing indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amendment permits an assessment of qualitative factors to determine whether the existence of events and circumstances indicates that it is more likely than not that the indefinite-lived intangible asset is impaired.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If, after assessing the totality of events and circumstances, it is concluded that it is not more likely than not that the indefinite-lived intangible asset is impaired, then no further action is required.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, after the same assessment, if it is concluded that it is more like than not that the indefinite-lived intangible asset is impaired, then a quantitative impairment test should be performed whereby the fair value of the indefinite-lived intangible asset is compared to the carrying amount.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amendments in this guidance are effective for annual and interim impairment tests performed for fiscal years beginning after September 15, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Early adoption is permitted.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The effect of adopting this standard did not have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s operating results or financial condition. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In February 2013, the FASB amended existing guidance related to reporting amounts reclassified out of other comprehensive income out of accumulated other comprehensive income.&#160; These amendments do not change the current requirements for reporting net income or other comprehensive income in financial statements. These amendments require an entity to provide information about the amounts reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income by component. In addition, an entity is required to present, either on the face of the statement where net income is presented or in the notes, significant amounts reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income by the respective line items of net income but only if the amount reclassified is required under U.S. GAAP to be reclassified to net income in its entirety in the same reporting period. For other amounts that are not required under U.S. GAAP to be reclassified in their entirety to net income, an entity is required to cross-reference to other disclosures required under U.S. GAAP that provide additional details about those amounts.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The effect of adopting this standard did not have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s operating results or financial condition. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 3 - LOANS</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> (Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Credit Quality Indicators:</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company categorizes loans into risk categories based on relevant information about the ability of borrowers to service their debt such as:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>current financial information, historical payment experience, credit documentation, public information, and current economic trends, among other factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company analyzes loans individually by classifying the loans as to credit risk.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This analysis includes loans with an outstanding balance greater than $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">100</FONT> and non-homogeneous loans, such as commercial and commercial real estate loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This analysis is performed on a quarterly basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company uses the following definitions for risk ratings:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Special Mention.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans classified as special mention have a potential weakness that deserves management's close attention. If left uncorrected, these potential weaknesses may result in deterioration of the repayment prospects for the loan or of the institution's credit position at some future date.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Substandard. </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT>Loans classified as substandard are inadequately protected by the current net worth and paying capacity of the obligor or of the collateral pledged, if any. Loans so classified have a well-defined weakness or weaknesses that jeopardize the liquidation of the debt. They are characterized by the distinct possibility that the institution will sustain some loss if the deficiencies are not corrected.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Doubtful.</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans classified as doubtful have all the weaknesses inherent in those classified as substandard, with the added characteristic that the weaknesses make collection or liquidation in full, on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions, and values, highly questionable and improbable.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans not meeting the criteria above that are analyzed individually as part of the above described process are considered to be pass rated loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans listed as not rated are either less than $100 or are included in group of homogeneous loans. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 9 - PREFERRED STOCK</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February&#160;13, 2009, the Company entered into a Letter Agreement (the &#8220;Purchase Agreement&#8221;) with the United States Department of Treasury (the &#8220;Treasury Department&#8221;) under the Troubled Asset Relief Program (&#8220;TARP&#8221;) Capital Purchase Program (&#8220;CPP&#8221;), pursuant to which the Company issued <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">34,000</FONT> shares of Series A Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock (the &#8220;Series A Preferred Stock&#8221;) for a total price of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">34</FONT> million.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Series A Preferred Stock is to pay cumulative dividends at an annual dividend rate of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">5</FONT>% for the first five years and thereafter at an annual dividend rate of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">9</FONT>%.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>No cash dividends can be paid to common stockholders unless all dividends on the Series A Preferred Stock have been declared and paid in full (or an amount sufficient for the payment of the dividends on the Series A Preferred Stock has been set aside for the payment of such dividends).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Pursuant to the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 (the &#8220;ARRA&#8221;), the Company may redeem the Series A Preferred Stock at any time, subject to the approval of its primary federal regulator.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As part of its purchase of the Series A Preferred Stock, the Treasury Department received a warrant (the &#8220;Warrant&#8221;) to purchase <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">274,784</FONT> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock at an initial per share exercise price of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">18.56</FONT>.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Warrant provides for the adjustment of the exercise price and the number of shares of common stock issuable upon exercise pursuant to customary anti-dilution provisions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Warrant expires ten years from the issuance date.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Both the Series A Preferred Stock and the Warrant are accounted for as components of Tier 1 capital.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The net proceeds received from the Treasury Department were allocated between the Series A Preferred Stock and Warrant based on relative fair value.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Series A Preferred Stock will be accreted to liquidation value over the expected life of the shares, with accretion charged to retained earnings. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 22, 2010, the Company repurchased $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">17</FONT> million of the outstanding $34 million of its Fixed Rate Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series A, issued in February 2009 to the Treasury Department pursuant to the Troubled Asset Relief Program Capital Purchase Program.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 23, 2011, the Company repurchased the final $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">17</FONT> million of the original outstanding $34 million of its Fixed Rate Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series A, issued in February 2009 to the Treasury Department pursuant to the Troubled Asset Relief Program Capital Purchase Program.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the second quarter of 2013, the Company completed the repurchase of the Warrant from the Treasury Department issued on February 13, 2009, as part of the TARP Capital Purchase Program for an aggregate repurchase price of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2,151</FONT>. Prior to the repurchase transaction, the Warrant permitted the Treasury Department to purchase 276,078.12 shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock at an exercise price of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">18.473</FONT> per share. The Warrant originally had provided for the purchase of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">274,784</FONT> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock at an exercise price of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">18.56</FONT> per share and was thereafter adjusted for certain cash dividends declared by the Company from time to time.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Warrant had been issued in connection with the Company&#8217;s sale to the Treasury Department of 34,000 shares of the Compnay&#8217;s Fixed Rate Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series A (the &#8220;Preferred Stock&#8221;) in 2009. As previously disclosed on the Company&#8217;s Current Report on Form 8-K filed Novemeber 23, 2011, the Company completed the repurchase of the remaining outstanding Preferred Stock from the Treasury Department on November 23, 2011. As a result of the Warrant repurchase, the Company has repurchased all securities issued to the Treasury Department&#160;under the TARP Capital Purchase Program.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The repurchase of the Warrant was funded by a $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2,000</FONT> note payable as described in Note 8.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 10 - EMPLOYEE BENEFITS</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank maintains an employee profit sharing plan covering substantially all employees.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Contributions are at the discretion of the Board of Directors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Profit sharing expense totaled $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">336</FONT>, $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">249</FONT>, and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">227</FONT> for the years ended December&#160;31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2003, the Company adopted a benefit program for certain officers to encourage long-term retention.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The program consists principally of a defined benefit component, providing each officer with payments equal to 30% of final average pay for 15 years after retirement, and a deferral component, permitting each officer the ability to defer a portion of their current compensation and earn pre-tax returns on such deferred amounts.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The accrued liability under the defined benefit component was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">4,884</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3,773</FONT> and the deferred compensation component was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,608</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,107</FONT> at December 31, 2013 and 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Expense related to the program was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,136</FONT>, $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">850</FONT>, and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">515</FONT> for the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 11 - STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Stock-based compensation in the form of options to buy stock and restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) are granted to directors, officers and employees under the Company&#8217;s incentive stock plan (the &#8220;Plan&#8221;), which provides for the issuance of up to <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,000,000</FONT> shares.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company believes that such awards better align the interests of its employees with those of its shareholders.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The specific terms of each option agreement are determined by the Compensation Committee at the date of the grant.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Stock Option Plan</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The specific terms of each option agreement are determined by the Compensation Committee at the date of the grant.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For current options outstanding, options granted to directors vest immediately and options granted to employees generally vest evenly over a five-year period.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
The options&#8217; lives are generally ten years for employees and five years for directors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Total compensation cost that has been charged against income for those plans was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">50</FONT>, $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">97</FONT>, and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">203</FONT> for 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The total income tax benefit was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">0</FONT>, $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">0</FONT>, and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">0</FONT>.</DIV>
</FONT>  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The fair value of each option award is estimated on the date of grant using a closed form option valuation (Black-Scholes) model that uses the assumptions noted in the table below.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Expected volatilities are based on historical volatilities of the Company&#8217;s common stock.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The risk-free interest rate for the expected term of the option is based on the U.S. Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of the grant.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Expected term is estimated based upon the contractual term and vesting period of the options including consideration of historical trends segregated by employees and directors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A forfeiture rate of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">19</FONT>% for employees and <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">0</FONT>% for directors is used in the model and is based on historical experience. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There have been no options granted in 2013, 2012, or 2011.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2013, there was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">39</FONT> of total unrecognized compensation cost related to nonvested stock options granted under the plan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.50</FONT> years. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Restricted Stock Units</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The specific terms of each restricted stock unit (&#8220;RSU&#8221;) award are determined by the Compensation Committee at the date of the grant.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Compensation expense is recognized over the vesting period of the awards based on the fair value of the stock at the issue date.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The fair value of the stock was determined using the total number of RSUs granted multiplied by the fair market value of a share of Company stock at the grant date.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>RSU&#8217;s are fully vested on the first anniversary of the grant date.<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></B></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Some financial instruments, such as loan commitments, credit lines, letters of credit, and overdraft protection, are issued to meet customer financing needs.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These are agreements to provide credit or to support the credit of others, so long as conditions established in the contract are met, and usually have expiration dates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Commitments may expire without being used.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Off-balance-sheet risk to credit loss exists up to the face amount of these instruments, although material losses are not anticipated.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The same credit policies are used to make such commitments as are used for loans, including obtaining collateral at exercise of the commitment.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 15 - INTEREST RATE CONTRACTS</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As a result of loans acquired through the Integra Bank transaction in the fourth quarter of 2010, the Bank initiated an interest rate protection program in which the Bank earns a fee by providing the Bank&#8217;s commercial loan customers the ability to swap from variable to fixed, or fixed to variable interest rates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under these agreements the Bank enters into a variable or fixed rate loan agreement with its customer in addition to a swap agreement.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The swap agreement effectively swaps the customer&#8217;s variable rate to a fixed rate or vice versa.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Bank then enters into a corresponding swap agreement with a third party in order to swap its exposure on the variable to fixed rate swap with the Bank&#8217;s customer.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Since the swaps are structured to offset each other, changes in fair values, while recorded, have no material net earnings impact.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The notional amount of interest rate swaps at December 31, 2013 was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">107,966</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">50,771</FONT> on December 31, 2012 with maturities ranging from one to ten years.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The current fair value of these swaps was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,915</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,926</FONT> at December 31, 2013 and 2012, respectively, and is included in other assets and other liabilities for the value of each of the swaps. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank is exposed to losses if a counterparty fails to make its payments under a contract in which the Bank is in the receiving status.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Although collateral or other security is not obtained, as the Bank is not currently in the receiving status, we minimize our credit risk by monitoring the credit standing of the counterparties.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We anticipate the counterparties will be able to fully satisfy their obligations under these agreements.</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="left">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 16 - CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS AND RESTRICTIONS ON RETAINED EARNINGS</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Banks and bank holding companies are subject to regulatory capital requirements administered by federal banking agencies.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Capital adequacy guidelines and, additionally for banks, prompt corrective action regulations, involve quantitative measures of assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance sheet items calculated under regulatory accounting practices.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgments by regulators.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Failure to meet capital requirements can initiate regulatory action.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management believes as of December 31, 2013, the Company and Bank meet all capital adequacy requirements to which they are subject.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Prompt corrective action regulations provide five classifications:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>well capitalized, adequately capitalized, undercapitalized, significantly undercapitalized, and critically undercapitalized, although these terms are not used to represent overall financial condition.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If adequately capitalized, regulatory approval is required to accept brokered deposits.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If undercapitalized, capital distributions are limited, as is asset growth and expansion, and capital restoration plans are required.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At year-end 2013 and 2012, the most recent regulatory notifications categorized the Bank as &#8220;well capitalized&#8221; under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There have been no subsequent conditions or events that management believes have changed the institution's category.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 17 - DISCLOSURES ABOUT FAIR VALUE </FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Accounting guidance establishes a fair value hierarchy which requires an entity to maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs when measuring fair value.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The standard describes three levels of inputs that may be used to measure fair value:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 1: Quoted prices (unadjusted) for identical assets or liabilities in active markets that the entity has the ability to access as of the measurement date.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 2: Significant other observable inputs other than Level 1 prices such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities; quoted prices in markets that are not active; or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 3: Significant unobservable inputs that reflect a reporting entity&#8217;s own assumptions about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or liability.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Investment Securities</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: The fair values of securities available-for-sale are determined by matrix pricing, which is a mathematical technique widely used in the industry to value debt securities without relying exclusively on quoted prices for the specific securities but rather by relying on the securities&#8217; relationship to other benchmark quoted securities (Level 2 inputs).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>One corporate security is valued using Level 3 inputs as there is no readily observable market activity.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management determines the value of this security based on expected cash flows, the credit quality of the security and current market interest rates.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Derivatives</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: The Bank&#8217;s derivative instruments consist of over-the-counter interest-rate swaps that trade in liquid markets.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The fair value of the derivative instruments is primarily measured by obtaining pricing from broker-dealers recognized to be market participants.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The pricing is derived from market observable inputs that can generally be verified and do not typically involve significant judgment by the Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This valuation method is classified as Level 2 in the fair value hierarchy.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>

  <TR>  <TD
style="BORDER-BOTTOM: windowtext 1pt solid; BORDER-LEFT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-BOTTOM: 0in; BACKGROUND-COLOR: transparent; PADDING-LEFT: 0in; WIDTH: 100%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0in; BORDER-TOP: #f0f0f0; BORDER-RIGHT: #f0f0f0; PADDING-TOP: 0in" valign="top" width="100%">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 17 - DISCLOSURES ABOUT FAIR VALUE </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued) </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Impaired Loans</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At the time a loan is considered impaired, it is recorded at the lower of cost or fair value.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Impaired loans carried at fair value generally receive specific allocations of the allowance for loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For collateral dependent loans, fair value is commonly based on recent real estate appraisals.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These appraisals may utilize a single valuation approach or a combination of approaches including comparable sales and the income approach.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Adjustments are routinely made in the appraisal process by the independent appraisers to adjust for differences between the comparable sales and income data available.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such adjustments are usually significant and typically result in a Level 3 classification of the inputs for determining fair value.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Non-real estate collateral may be valued using an appraisal, net book value per the borrower&#8217;s financial statements or aging reports, adjusted or discounted based on management&#8217;s historical knowledge, changes in market conditions from the time of the valuation and management&#8217;s expertise and knowledge of the client and client&#8217;s business, resulting in a Level 3 fair value classification.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;The standard&#160;discount on equipment, accounts receivable, and inventory is <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">50</FONT>%. &#160;</FONT>Impaired loans are evaluated on a quarterly basis for additional impairment and adjusted accordingly.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other Real Estate Owned</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Assets acquired through or instead of loan foreclosure are initially recorded at fair value less costs to sell when acquired, establishing a new cost basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These assets are subsequently accounted for at the lower of cost or fair value less estimated costs to sell. Fair value is commonly based on recent real estate appraisals.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These appraisals may utilize a single valuation approach or a combination of approaches including comparable sales and the income approach.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Adjustments are routinely made in the appraisal process by the independent appraisers to adjust for differences between the comparable sales and income data available.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such adjustments are usually significant and typically result in a Level 3 classification of the inputs for determining fair value.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans Held For Sale</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans held for sale are carried at the lower of cost or fair value, which is evaluated on a pool-level basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The fair value of loans held for sale is determined using quoted prices for similar assets, adjusted for specific attributes of that loan or other observable market data, such as outstanding commitments from third party investors (Level 2).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Impaired loans, which are measured for impairment using the fair value of the collateral for collateral dependent loans, had a gross carrying amount of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">17,600</FONT> with a valuation allowance of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3,419</FONT>, resulting in a decrease in provision for loan losses of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2,846</FONT> for 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As of December 31, 2012, impaired loans had a gross carrying amount of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">27,548</FONT>, with a valuation allowance of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">6,265</FONT>, resulting in an decrease in provision for loan losses of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,178</FONT>. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other real estate owned measured at fair value less costs to sell, had a net carrying amount of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2,772</FONT>, which is made up of the outstanding balance of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3,287</FONT>, net of a valuation allowance of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">515</FONT> at December 31, 2013 resulting in a write-down of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">263</FONT>, for the year ended December 31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At December 31, 2012, other real estate owned had a net carrying amount of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3,079</FONT>, made up of the outstanding balance of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3,728</FONT>, net of a valuation allowance of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">649</FONT>, resulting in a write-down of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">369</FONT> for the year ended December 31, 2012. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Values for collateral dependent loans and other real estate owned are generally based on appraisals obtained from licensed real estate appraisers and in certain circumstances consideration of offers obtained to purchase properties prior to foreclosure or other factors management deems relevant to arrive at a representative fair value. &#160;Appraisals for commercial real estate generally use three methods to derive value: cost, sales or market comparison and income approach. &#160;The cost method bases value on the cost to replace the current property. &#160;The market comparison approach evaluates the sales price of similar properties in the same market area. &#160;The income approach considers net operating income generated by the property and an investor&#8217;s required return. &#160;The final fair value is based on a reconciliation of these three approaches.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Values for non real estate collateral, such as business equipment, are based on the licensed real estate appraisals valuation or the customer&#8217;s financial statements.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Values for the non real estate collateral use much higher discounts than does real estate collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This is reflected in the high discount rate used on Commercial loans which have a much higher percentage of equipment collateral than other loan types have.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 17 - DISCLOSURES ABOUT FAIR VALUE</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> (Continued)&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The estimated fair value approximates carrying amounts for all items except those described below.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The carrying amounts of cash and short-term instruments approximate fair values and are classified as either Level 1 or Level 2.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Estimated fair value for both securities available-for-sale and held-to-maturity is as previously described for securities available-for-sale.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It is not practicable to determine the fair value of Federal Home Loan Bank stock due to restrictions placed on its transferability.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Fair values of loans, excluding loans held for sale, are estimated as set forth below: </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The methods and assumptions, not previously presented, used to estimate fair values are described as follows:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Cash and cash equivalents</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: The carrying amounts of cash and cash equivalents approximate fair values and are classified as Level 1. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Interest-bearing deposits with banks</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: The carrying amount of interest-bearing deposits equivalents approximate fair value and are classified a Level 1.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Federal Home Loan Bank stock</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: It is not practicable to determine the fair value of Federal Home Loan Bank stock due to restrictions placed on its transferability. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans held for sale</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: The fair value of loans held for sale is estimated based upon binding contracts and quotes from third party investors resulting in a Level 2 classification.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans, net</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: For variable rate loans that reprice frequently and with no significant change in credit risk, fair values are based on carrying values resulting in a Level 3 classification. Fair values for other loans are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses, using interest rates currently being offered for loans with similar terms to borrowers of similar credit quality resulting in a Level 3 classification.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Impaired loans are valued at the lower of cost or fair value as described previously.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The methods utilized to estimate the fair value of loans do not necessarily represent an exit price.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Accrued interest receivable/payable</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: The carrying amounts of accrued interest approximate fair value resulting in a Level 1, Level 2 or Level 3 classification consistent with the classification of the asset/liability with which they are associated.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Deposits</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: The fair values disclosed for demand deposits (e.g., interest and non-interest checking, passbook savings and certain types of money market accounts) are, by definition, equal to the amount payable on demand at the reporting date (i.e., their carrying amount) resulting in a Level 1 classification. The carrying amounts of variable rate, fixed-term money market accounts and certificates of deposit approximate their fair values at the reporting date resulting in a Level 2 classification. Fair values for fixed rate certificates of deposit are estimated using a discounted cash flows calculation that applies interest rates currently being offered on certificates to a schedule of aggregated expected monthly maturities on time deposits resulting in a Level 2 classification. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued)</FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTE 17 - DISCLOSURES ABOUT FAIR VALUE </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Continued) </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Short-term borrowings</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: The carrying amounts of short-term borrowings, generally maturing within ninety days, approximate their fair values resulting in a Level 2 classification. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Notes payable</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The carrying amounts of borrowings under repurchase agreements approximate their fair values resulting in a Level 2 classification. The fair values of the Company&#8217;s long-term borrowings are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses based on the current borrowing rates for similar types of borrowing arrangements resulting in a Level 2 classification.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The fair values of the Company&#8217;s </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">subordinated debentures are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses based on the current borrowing rates for similar types of borrowing arrangements resulting in a Level 3 classification.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Standby letters of credit and off-balance sheet instruments</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: Fair values for off-balance sheet, credit-related financial instruments are based on fees currently charged to enter into similar agreements, taking into account the remaining terms of the agreements and the counterparties&#8217; credit standing, which results in a level 3 classification. The fair value of commitments is not material. Estimated fair value of standby letters of credit are based on their current unearned fee balance. Estimated fair value for commitments to make loans and unused lines of credit are considered nominal.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
